```
## W5. Factbase & Analytics Consolidation — regular routine

Runs weekly (Sunday, after W4). **Repurposed 2026-06-06 (BigQuery cutover §15):** the Decision_Log live/archive prune is RETIRED — `events.decision_log` holds everything, queryable + bounded, so there is nothing to archive. W5 is now **weekly knowledge + analytics consolidation**: extract new Strategy-B sub-patterns, capture protocol revisions, reconcile the Watchlist, and report historical calibration/reconciliation trends. It does not repair embeddings or investigate live account drift; D2a and the daily monitors own those operational controls. Not deep research.

```
Read access scope: Weekly cadence with factbase WRITE permission. Query `events.decision_log` (entries added since the last W5 run, by `entry_date`/`event_ts`), `analytics.calibration_summary`, historical `analytics.account_reconciliation` trends, and `state.current_positions`. Read the kept factbase/spec files `B_Sub_Pattern_Taxonomy.md`, `Watchlist.md`, `Operating_Protocols.md`.

**SAME-DAY DOUBLE-RUN GUARD (completeness-critic N-4, 2026-07-16 — see the shared Observability section's generalized guard)** — FIRST, before the dependency gate below, before anything else: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ops.run_log WHERE routine='W5' AND run_date=<today, America/Denver> AND status='completed'`; if `>= 1`, output "W5 already completed today (a prior fire — OPS0 catch-up or W5's own scheduled trigger — already completed; this is the expected redundant re-invocation, not an error)." and END IMMEDIATELY — do NOT redo the consolidation, do NOT log another `started`/`completed` row.

**DEPENDENCY GATE — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap — `CALL ops.sp_assert_deps('W5', ['W4'], <today>)` BEFORE the start-log, before anything else in this routine.** Aborts (RAISE) + raises a `missing_dependency` critical if W4 has no `completed` run anywhere in the current weekly period — W4 is `weekly_sun`, so since `bigquery/114_period_aware_dependency_gate.sql` (2026-07-29) the gate is satisfied by any W4 completion with `run_date BETWEEN` that week's Sunday `AND` today, not only a completion on this exact calendar day (this is also what fixed the pre-existing false-positive on a W5 running Monday against a Sunday-completed W4); self-bootstrapping. This is the general rule from Observability § above, restated here because it is the one call in this routine that must never be skipped (a 2026-07-09 audit found an analogous D2 session skip this exact call for its own dependency, so it is now inlined per-routine rather than left to a shared preamble alone).

FACTBASE MIRRORING — walk the new `events.decision_log` entries since the last W5 run and mirror durable signal into the kept factbase files.

Mirror to `Watchlist.md`:
- For any entry that adds a name to a strategy queue (e.g., "AAPL added to A-watchlist queue per router-gate-failure pattern"), ensure the name appears in Watchlist.md under the appropriate strategy section. Per-name fields: ticker, date-added, source-`events.decision_log`-entry-date, reason summary, resolution-trigger condition (e.g., "next M1 with A router ACTIVATE").
- For any entry that resolves a queue item (e.g., a future thesis-construction session that processes a queued name), ensure the resolved name is removed from Watchlist.md.
- Do NOT add Strategy B prior-NO-GO names to Watchlist.md — B operates on event-flow with fresh evaluation per "NO-GO records are context, not barriers". Sub-pattern factbase preserves the durable signal.
- Do NOT add Strategy D pending re-screens to Watchlist.md — calendar events are the canonical source.
- Note: Watchlist.md is also written by D2 / M4 (action-conversion routines) and W4 (queue-only research handoff) for in-cycle additions; W5 reconciles any drift between those writes and `events.decision_log` signal.

Mirror to `Operating_Protocols.md`:
- For any entry that introduces or revises an operational protocol (operating-model updates, commission-disregarded protocol, "NO-GO records are context, not barriers" rule, conviction-calibration ladder, deferral chaining rules, file-conventions/read-access-scope policy, decision-log lifecycle policy, etc.), ensure the canonical-current text is reflected in Operating_Protocols.md. Each protocol gets a section with: title, current canonical text, revision-history list (date + `events.decision_log` entry pointer + brief change description per revision).
- When revising an existing protocol section, replace the canonical text with the new revision and append the prior canonical to revision history.
- Do NOT mirror NO-GO entries, position entries, calendar-recon entries, or session-end-consolidation entries — those are not protocol entries.
Mirror to `strategy/roster.yaml` (rev 2026-07-10 — Strategy Arsenal autonomy conversion, owner directive):
- For any `events.strategy_lifecycle` / roster transition in `events.decision_log` since the last W5 run (CANDIDATE / QUALIFYING / AUTHORING / UNDER_REVIEW / SHADOW / PAPER / PROBE / ADOPTED / RETIREMENT_PROPOSED / TERMINATED / POST_MORTEM / REJECTED), append a dated entry to the affected strategy's `revision_history:` list in `strategy/roster.yaml` (date + lifecycle event + `git_commit` + one-line note) — exactly the mirroring pattern this routine uses for Operating_Protocols.md protocol revisions. SL5 is the authoritative writer of roster MEMBERSHIP and the `roster_state` field; W5 only keeps the human-readable `revision_history` in sync and NEVER flips a `roster_state` itself.
- W5 is aware of `scripts/check_roster_consistency.py` (the roster analog of `check_cadence_consistency.py`): if a mirrored edit would make `strategy/roster.yaml` disagree with `state.strategy_roster` / the Strategy.md `## Strategy` sections / the slice-map, do NOT commit the drift — log a consistency-check anomaly (the CI gate would fail the build anyway, and auto-merge only merges on green CI).

ANALYTICS REVIEW (BigQuery) — the Decision_Log live/archive split + weekly prune is RETIRED (`events.decision_log` is queryable + bounded; nothing to archive). Instead:
- **Embedding trend only.** Routine-side `ops.sp_log_decision` embeds inline; pending/error detection and remediation are daily operational concerns. W5 may report the historical weekly embedding-health trend in its outcome, but performs no embedding maintenance.
- Review `analytics.calibration_shrunk` (self-improvement audit S-2/B-2, 2026-07-03 — supersedes reading `analytics.calibration_summary` alone) — per-conviction-tier `win_rate_shrunk` (Beta-Binomial posterior, honest-wide at low N) + `wilson_low`/`wilson_high` + `trustworthy_edge`. Log a one-line note to `events.decision_log` of the current per-tier posterior + interval width; this is the calibration signal any future thesis-construction session should read, NOT the raw `win_rate` column (which reads 1.000 on a small all-wins tier and is the exact overfitting hazard the foundation doc warns against). The BQML `conviction_model` (bigquery/04_analytics.sql, gated at ≥30 closed) is DEPRECATED — a logistic fit on ~30 fee-dominated, single-class, non-independent (one regime, correlated) binary outcomes with 4 categorical features and no CV/walk-forward would overfit; `calibration_shrunk` dominates it and needs no both-classes precondition. Do not build or gate on the BQML model even once 30 closed trades accrue.
- **Historical reconciliation reporting only.** Summarize week-over-week reconciliation/NAV history for learning and trend context, but do not diagnose a live discrepancy, raise an operational drift alert, or attempt a repair. D2a's daily broker reconciliation and its daily monitors are the sole operational owners of current account drift.
- **WASH-SALE EXPOSURE REVIEW (self-improvement audit ITEM 18, 2026-07-11).** **BACK-DATED PARK ROWS — ONE-TIME FULL SWEEP (2026-08-18).** `bigquery/178_park_wash_sale_exposure.sql` extends this view to cover park (`close_strategy='PARK'`) round trips, which were structurally invisible to it before (park fills live in `events.parking_events`, never in `events.trade_fills`). Those rows arrive ALREADY BACK-DATED — the first real one is the 2026-07-27 VOO liquidation, ~$78 of loss repurchased 2026-08-04 — so the "dated since the last W5 run" filter below would skip every one of them forever and this fix would land in the table without ever reaching the operator. Therefore: on the first W5 run that sees ANY `close_strategy='PARK'` row, ignore the date filter for park rows specifically and report the FULL park history once, then revert to the normal since-last-run behaviour (mechanically self-terminating: once reported, the prior `wash-sale-review` decision_log entry names those `close_trade_id`s, so a later run can tell already-reported park rows from genuinely new ones and must report only the latter). Read `state.wash_sale_exposure` (`bigquery/41_tax_lots.sql`, extended by `bigquery/178`) for any exposure rows dated since the last W5 run — a BUY within 30 calendar days of any strategy's loss-realizing SELL in the same ticker, ACROSS strategies (the roster's `n_max=8` ceiling means this experiment deliberately runs multiple strategies that can independently trade the same name; a per-strategy view cannot see this). Log a one-line note to `events.decision_log` (`entry_type='wash-sale-review'`) summarizing new-since-last-run exposure rows (ticker, strategies involved, estimated disallowed-loss amount); if any row is new since the last W5 run, `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','W5','wash_sale_exposure','<ticker + strategies + estimated disallowed amount>','<JSON>')` so it reaches the monitored alert channel. **`_once`, not the plain `sp_raise_alert` this step used until 2026-08-25.** The step's self-termination guarantee rested entirely on a future memoryless session correctly diffing the prior cycle's `close_trade_id`s out of its own report; with the plain raise there was no dedup backstop if that prose-following ever slipped, and a duplicate exposure alert would simply be inserted. Keep the varying dollar amounts in the JSON payload and the message text stable per `(ticker, strategies)`, since `sp_raise_alert_once` dedups on the exact `(category, message)` text. Detection/reporting only — this never blocks a trade or a kill-trigger action (IBKR's own 1099-B, computed off the elected cost-basis method, remains the authoritative tax figure); it exists so the accumulating disallowed-loss exposure is visible before year-end rather than discovered on the 1099-B.
- Review `analytics.process_scorecard` (self-improvement audit S-7/B-9, 2026-07-03) — decision-quality signals that accrue per-decision, not per rare close: `conviction_tiers_observed` / `analytics.conviction_monotonicity` (does higher stated conviction rank-order higher realized P&L — read as raw per-tier counts, directional only, never a trigger), `go_minus_opened` (a large gap between GO theses and positions actually opened flags a staging-pipeline issue worth a look), and `forecast_pct_below_band` (is the M5 TWR forecast systematically biased — advisory only, per bigquery/06_forecast.sql). Each metric carries its own `min_n_met` floor; below it, log the observation but do not treat it as signal. AUTONOMOUS ROUTING (rev 2026-07-10 — round-2 conversion): a detected staging-pipeline gap must NOT dead-end as a chat note a human is expected to "take a look" at. For any metric with `min_n_met=TRUE` whose reading is out of band (e.g. `go_minus_opened` materially positive), log the finding to `events.decision_log` AND `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','W5','process_scorecard_signal','<metric + value + strategy>','<JSON>')` so it reaches the monitored alert channel rather than an unread chat surface (severity bumped info→warning 2026-07-16, consumption-closure CC-7 — `info` is filtered by both `alert_emailer.gs` and `alert_relay.py`, so this alert never actually reached any monitored channel until now); `forecast_pct_below_band` stays advisory (log-only) per bigquery/06_forecast.sql.
- **CAPITAL-UTILISATION & RESTORE-INTEGRITY REVIEW (2026-08-11, `bigquery/164_capital_utilisation_and_restore_integrity.sql`).** Three read-only checks on whether the capital model is still doing what Experiment_Parameters.md says it does — reward winners passively via survivorship. All three are WARNING-class and none can halt trading.
  1. `SELECT * FROM state.capital_utilisation_watch` — one row per capital-ENABLED strategy. For any row with `is_stranded = TRUE`, `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','W5','capital_stranded','<strategy + idle_capital + days_since_deployment>','<TO_JSON_STRING of the row>')`. **Read the `posture` column before acting.** A strategy that is idle but has a non-zero `evaluations_60d` is HEALTHY — Operating_Protocols §16 says an active strategy that is merely idle keeps its capital, and declining a thesis on its own mechanical criteria IS the strategy working. `is_stranded` deliberately fires only when idle capital is material AND there has been no deployment for 90+ days AND nothing has evaluated the strategy in 60 days. Do NOT widen this predicate to "idle capital alone"; it would fire on every healthy low-frequency strategy from day one and be muted within a week.
  2. `SELECT * FROM state.regime_restore_shortfall_risk` — the swept-capital debt against what the enabled donors could actually return. On `aggregate_at_risk` or `at_risk_including_newcomer_claim`, `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','W5','regime_restore_shortfall','<total debt + donor capacity + shortfall>','<JSON>')`. **Read "shortfall" as THIS SESSION'S shortfall, not a loss.** `bigquery/98`'s restore trigger is a standing condition (any enabled strategy with `outstanding_debt > 0`, re-evaluated on every read, no transition gate, no cooldown, no retry guard), so an unpaid residual is re-proposed automatically as donor capacity recovers — the `>=$25-or-full-debt` floor only defers a sub-$25 tail, it cannot strand it. So this alert means "a re-enabled strategy is trading on a fraction of its owed capital right now," not "capital was lost." That is still worth surfacing, because an under-capitalised debtor is otherwise invisible — it just quietly trades smaller than it should, and nobody would connect that to a sweep weeks earlier. The view also nets the SISA pending-newcomer probe-stake claim, because newcomers outrank the restore on every inflow and nothing else shows the two claims against one pool.
  3. `SELECT * FROM state.sweep_recipient_weights` — informational this run. It precomputes the mechanical, judgment-free capacity tilt (share of the trailing 180 days each recipient actually held a position, mapped onto §16's sanctioned [0.5x, 2x] band) that a future D2a SWEEP substep may apply instead of DEFAULT-EQUAL. No alert; log the reading if `sweep_share` diverges materially from `equal_share`, since that is the first evidence the tilt would change an outcome.
- **EXTERNAL-SPEND DIGEST (2026-08-17, `bigquery/174_web_call_telemetry.sql` — the consumer that closes the shared "Metered external calls" rule's part (d)).** Read BOTH: `SELECT * FROM state.web_spend_month WHERE month_start >= DATE_TRUNC(DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE('America/Denver'), INTERVAL 60 DAY), MONTH)` (per `(month, provider, routine)` call counts and credits) **and `SELECT * FROM state.web_duplicate_targets ORDER BY credits_on_repeats DESC LIMIT 25`** — both over `ops.web_calls`. Log one `events.decision_log` entry via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` with `entry_type='external-spend-digest'`, naming the current month's fleet total per provider, the top 3 routines by `credits`, and — **the finding that actually matters** — the top repeat-fetched targets with their `credits_on_repeats` and whether each is `is_cross_routine`. **A cross-routine repeat is the highest-value one to report**: neither routine can see the other doing it, so it is the class that persists indefinitely unnoticed, and it is the concrete instance of the shared rule's "the one thing that IS waste." **ALSO NAME THE PRICED-DEPTH SHARE, which this digest has never reported even though the column already exists (added 2026-08-21, external-spend audit).** `state.web_spend_month` already computes `n_priced_upgrade` (`bigquery/174_web_call_telemetry.sql`) and nothing has ever read it, so the second of the two levers the shared rule's baseline note itself names — "search COUNT and search DEPTH, in that order" — is measured, stored, and then left out of the only report that reads this table. Per `(month, routine)`, state `n_priced_upgrade` as a share of that routine's Tavily searches together with the credits attributable to the upgrade (advanced bills 2 credits to basic's 1, so the upgrade's own cost in credits equals `n_priced_upgrade`), and say when that share MOVED rather than only where it stands: measured across the 171 logged Tavily calls to 2026-08-21, 95 were advanced (55.6%) = 95 of 252.4 logged credits, **38% of logged Tavily spend**, and the rate swung from 14% advanced on the 2026-08-19 D1 run (8 of 57 searches) to 76% on 2026-08-20 (54 of 71) across two consecutive runs with no recorded reason — the swing is the reportable finding, not the level. Same FLOOR caveat as (1) below: this share is computed over LOGGED calls only. **RECORD-ONLY — no threshold, no alert, no cap; nothing here gates anything and W5 never edits a token. Specifically, this share is NOT a proposal to disable `auto_parameters=true` or to force basic depth** — that setting is ENDORSED by owner directive 2026-08-17 (the session picks depth per task, paying 2 credits when that is the better answer), and a depth cap read out of this number would be exactly the unfounded knob the "no per-routine credit cap from spend alone" rule below refuses. Two honesty requirements, both binding: (1) **report `has_unreported_runs`** — where TRUE, that routine logged completed runs that emitted no token, so its credits are a **FLOOR, not a total**; name those routines rather than quoting a fleet figure that reads as complete; (2) per the shared rule this series is a **self-reported ESTIMATE, not a meter** (no usage endpoint exists on the Tavily MCP surface), so the provider's own dashboard stays authoritative for the account total — state the estimate as an estimate and never reconcile the two silently. **Do not propose a per-routine credit cap from fewer than two COMPLETE months of tokens.** The series exists precisely to make such a cap evidence-based; a first partial month is the noise the sibling process-reliability loop's 3-consecutive-cycle persistence bar exists to reject, and the same discipline binds here.
- **PROCESS-RELIABILITY REVIEW (self-improvement audit WO-6, 2026-07-03; active_auto per `ops/autonomy_levels.yaml`, loop `process_reliability`; rev 2026-07-10b — stage bumped to match ceiling, code-review finding #7, owner-confirmed. The loop's OWN data-sufficiency gate below — not a separate stage check — governs whether it does anything on a given firing).** First, the ALWAYS-autonomous fail-safe check (unconditional, runs before anything else in this bullet): read `state.process_constant_oos_watch` (bigquery/72_constant_tuning_oos_watch.sql); for any `degraded_revert = TRUE` row, auto-REVERT the constant to `old_value` (edit the version-controlled deadline/threshold back, run `check_cadence_consistency.py`, commit + push, auto-merge on green CI), `INSERT` an `ops.process_constant_change_log` row with `change_key = CONCAT(<original change_key>, ':REVERT')` (and the same routine/deadline_key, old/new swapped), log `events.decision_log`, and `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','W5','process_constant_reverted','<routine + deadline_key + restored value + post-change threat evidence>','<JSON>')` — a post-change threat recurrence means the relaxation was chasing a drifting routine; restoring the tighter deadline is the fail-safe direction (the watchdog alarms instead of being quietly loosened). Then read `analytics.routine_health_scorecard` (canonical definition bigquery/89 as of 2026-07-18, superseding bigquery/27): per-routine 90-day completion/failure/halt counts, p50/p90 completion minutes (midnight-safe as of bigquery/89 — computed as minutes since 00:00 of `run_date`, so a past-midnight completion reads >1440 instead of wrapping to near-zero), dep-gate abort count, and the retry-telemetry columns (`n_retry_events`, `n_retries_exhausted`, `n_dep_waits`, `n_dep_wait_futile`, `n_active_refires`, `total_wait_minutes` — from `state.retry_telemetry`, bigquery/88). EVERY W5 cycle, append one observation row per routine to `ops.process_reliability_observations` (INSERT — this is both the loop heartbeat and the persistence substrate; **set `cycle_date` = this W5 cycle's run_date in `America/Denver`, per the column's own DDL comment — NOT NULL, no default, and the PARTITION key, so an omitted value fails the INSERT outright and an invented UTC date silently mis-buckets the cycle across the two-hour band the OPERATING-plane pin exists to prevent (pinned 2026-08-19; neither this bullet nor its `ops.research_quality_observations` twin named the column)**) recording whether the routine currently shows the deadline-threat pattern: `min_n_met=TRUE` AND `p90_completion_minute_of_day` within ~90 minutes of a version-controlled deadline it could plausibly threaten (e.g. the `cadence_watch_deadline_local` 21:00 MT guard in `ops/cadence.yaml`), with `deadline_key` naming that constant, and summarize the routine's retry-telemetry columns in the observation's `note`. **Two v2 discounts when judging threat_pattern (2026-07-18 adversarial review):** (1) lateness EXPLAINED BY DELIBERATE PROTOCOL WAITING is not drift — if the routine's `total_wait_minutes`/`n_dep_waits` show material DEPENDENCY-WAIT/retry activity in the window, discount the wait time from its effective lateness before comparing against the deadline (a routine that completes late BECAUSE it correctly waited out a late upstream must not get the watchdog deadline quietly moved for it); (2) any 3-consecutive-cycle streak whose trailing window includes cycles computed BEFORE the bigquery/89 metric redefinition (landed 2026-07-18; see the `events.decision_log` ops entry) is NOT valid evidence for `ready_for_change` on completion-time grounds — the redefinition can reveal a pre-existing past-midnight backlog in one step, which is a measurement correction, not three weeks of fresh drift; restart the streak count from the first post-redefinition cycle. Then read `SELECT * FROM state.process_reliability_readiness` (bigquery/37_self_improvement_autonomy.sql). If `ready_for_change = FALSE` (the expected state until the threat pattern has persisted on the 3 most-recent consecutive cycles), log the observation to `events.decision_log` and do nothing else — NOT a finding, no chat mention. 4. Mechanical-failure NO-GOs (criterion-1 mechanical, instrument-rule, router-gate failures): no sub-pattern extraction needed.

**NO-GO COUNTERFACTUAL SHADOW-TRACKING (self-improvement audit S-3, 2026-07-03) — makes step 3 above bidirectional.** The taxonomy above records only avoided trades; it never checks whether the avoided name actually underperformed, which is pure survivorship/confirmation-bias exposure. Two sub-steps, both best-effort (a connector hiccup must never abort W5). **Price sourcing (rewired 2026-07-19: IBKR-primary after FMP free-tier re-scope; owner-approved):** IBKR is PRIMARY — resolve the shadow ticker via `search_contracts` (exact-symbol row, US primary listing) and read `get_price_snapshot`'s `last` (when the market is closed, `last`/`prior_close` is the prior close — fine for a weekly shadow mark); `mcp__FMP__quote` is a best-effort FALLBACK only, and now works only for FMP's free-list symbols (~87 big-caps + 9 indexes) since FMP's 2026-07-19 free-tier re-scoping symbol-blocked the rest:
   a. **Log new shadow rows.** For each new criterion-4 NO-GO extracted in step 3 above (a genuine sub-pattern classification, not a mechanical NO-GO): fetch the ticker's current price per the sourcing note above, then `INSERT INTO events.nogo_shadow (decision_log_entry_id, ticker, sub_pattern, nogo_date, entry_ref_price)` (`horizon_days` defaults to 21 — leave it unless the thesis window implies otherwise). `bigquery/28_nogo_shadow.sql`.
   b. **Close out elapsed shadow rows.** Query `SELECT * FROM events.nogo_shadow WHERE forward_price IS NULL AND DATE_ADD(nogo_date, INTERVAL horizon_days DAY) <= CURRENT_DATE('America/Denver')`. For each: fetch the ticker's current price per the sourcing note above and `UPDATE events.nogo_shadow SET forward_price = <price>, forward_price_date = CURRENT_DATE('America/Denver') WHERE event_id = <id>` (a `SELECT`-then-`INSERT`-corrected-row pattern is fine too since this table is a low-volume shadow log, not the append-only trading truth — it is explicitly a mutable tracking table, not one of the audit-trail tables `state.append_only_integrity` watches).
   c. **Read the tally, update the taxonomy.** Read **`analytics.nogo_counterfactual_by_primary`** (`bigquery/152`, per-PRIMARY-token `n_correct`/`n_incorrect`/`n_closed_unscored`/`min_n_met` — excess return vs SGOV, never raw price, so a rising-market false "wrong NO-GO" reading is avoided). **Read the by-primary view, NOT `analytics.nogo_counterfactual_summary`, for the `min_n_met` decision below** (2026-08-09, W5): the older summary groups on the RAW decorated `sub_pattern` string, and because the controlled vocabulary appends variant letters, ` (candidate)` and ` [overlay: …]` composites, 37 shadow rows fragmented into 33 single-row buckets — its `>=5 closed-out` floor was **structurally unreachable**, so this demotion branch could never fire. `nogo_counterfactual_by_primary` groups at the grain `B_Sub_Pattern_Taxonomy.md` already documents (`REGEXP_EXTRACT(sub_pattern, r'^(SP[0-9]+|PatternN|Mechanical)')`) and collapses the same 37 rows to 13 tokens. The raw-grain summary view is kept, unchanged, for the finer per-composite detail. Also check `n_closed_unscored`: a NON-ZERO value there means closed rows whose excess return could not be computed, which is the failure mode that hid the 2026-07-19..2026-08-09 outage (a NULL scored in neither direction and read as "no signal yet" rather than "never scored") — investigate it rather than reading the tally as complete. For any sub-pattern with `min_n_met = TRUE` (>=5 closed-out) and `n_incorrect > n_correct`, append a note to that sub-pattern's B_Sub_Pattern_Taxonomy.md section: "counterfactual tally: X/Y NO-GOs where the avoided name subsequently underperformed SGOV — below-chance, candidate for taxonomy review" — an autonomously-actioned taxonomy update, NOT a chat/human-visible flag someone must resolve (rev 2026-07-10 — round-2 conversion). The N-floor caveat is PRESERVED as the data gate: a below-chance tally at N<15-20 can still be noise, so while 5<=N<15-20 the note above stays informational-only and routing is NOT down-weighted. Once a sub-pattern reaches N>=15-20 closed-out shadow rows still with `n_incorrect > n_correct`, the loop SELF-APPLIES the down-weight with NO human taxonomy-review step: change that note to a dated `DEMOTED — routing down-weighted` entry, commit + push (auto-merge on green CI), log an `events.decision_log` entry, and `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('info','W5','nogo_subpattern_demoted','<sub-pattern + X/Y tally>','<JSON>')`.

**DECISION-LOG VOCABULARY DRIFT WATCH (added 2026-07-30, decision-record audit).** W5 already owns controlled-vocabulary hygiene for `sub_pattern` (ops/RUNBOOK.md §21 — the one sanctioned in-place-UPDATE exception, and W5 conforms any drift). Extend that ownership to the two columns the learning views actually key on, which had NO owner and no check at all. This is a ROUTINE-side watch by necessity, not a CI gate: this repo's CI checkers are static offline text parsers with no live BigQuery access (only the keyless-WIF `warehouse-validation` job touches the warehouse), so nothing in CI can see a bad value that only exists as data.

Query the vocabulary actually in use since the last W5 run:

```sql
SELECT entry_type, decision, COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(entry_date) AS first_seen, MAX(entry_date) AS last_seen
FROM `stock-trading-498512.events.decision_log`
WHERE entry_date > <last W5 run date>
GROUP BY entry_type, decision ORDER BY n DESC
```

Check BOTH DIRECTIONS. Checking only one is how the 2026-07-20..22 incident stayed invisible for months:

**(a) WRONGLY EXCLUDED (false negative)** — a value not in the controlled vocabulary, which a view's filter therefore drops. This is the entry_type='thesis' case.

**(b) WRONGLY INCLUDED (false positive)** — a value that a view's filter MATCHES but that is not in the sanctioned set. This direction exists because `analytics.thesis_outcomes.is_go_family` is a `^GO\b` PREFIX test, which is strictly more permissive than the two-value GO family it is meant to recognise: verified live that `'GO/NO-GO'`, `'GO-WITHOUT-ORDER'`, `'GO-AHEAD'`, `'GO,'` and `'GO (partial)'` would all match. Any of those would be counted as a GO observation in calibration AND would pass the campaign-join guard that exists to stop a non-GO thesis inheriting a real position's realized P&L. Run:

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT decision FROM `stock-trading-498512.events.decision_log`
WHERE entry_type IN ('thesis-construction','thesis')
  AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(UPPER(TRIM(COALESCE(decision,''))), r'^GO\b')
  AND UPPER(TRIM(decision)) NOT IN ('GO', 'GO (ADD TRANCHE)')
```

Any row returned is a false positive already accruing into calibration — treat as CRITICAL, not a warning, and tighten `is_go_family` to an explicit allowlist in a new numbered `bigquery/` file in the same session.

For any value found in EITHER direction: **do not attempt to UPDATE the rows** (append-only; only `sub_pattern` has an exception, and a second standing exception was explicitly declined — ops/RUNBOOK.md §44). Instead, in the same W5 session: (i) determine whether any learning view's filter silently excludes it — check `analytics.thesis_outcomes`, `analytics.conviction_features`, `analytics.thesis_outcome_summary` for the affected row; (ii) if it IS excluded, widen the relevant view's synonym tolerance in a NEW numbered `bigquery/` file, apply it live, and mirror the change into the dbt model so the dbt-parity row-level check stays green; (iii) correct the emitting routine's text here so the drift stops at source; (iv) `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('info','W5','decision_vocab_drift','<the value + affected view>','<JSON>')` and log it in the W5 outcome entry. Self-executed, no chat step.

WHY this is worth a weekly query: the 2026-07-20..22 `entry_type='thesis'` incident ran for three days, self-corrected, and was never noticed — it took a dedicated audit four months later to find that a real Strategy B GO had been invisible to every calibration view the whole time. `analytics.thesis_outcomes.paired_by_fk` and the drift query above are the two cheap telemetry reads that would have surfaced it in a week.

QUARTER ROLLOVER: RETIRED — the per-quarter Decision_Log archive files are gone (`events.decision_log` holds all history, queryable + bounded by `event_ts`), so there is no archive file to close out or start at quarter rollover.

ENTRIES THAT POINT BACKWARDS: when an `events.decision_log` entry contains "References" pointing to specific other entries, leave the references as-is (text-level). The structured fields (entry id / date+title) make lookup deterministic by query.

CONSISTENCY CHECK: cross-reference text mentioning specific dated entries (e.g. "per Decision_Log 2026-04-29 SBUX NO-GO") is fine — the reader can find the row by query. Do NOT mass-rewrite cross-references. (There is no live/archive split to keep consistent — `events.decision_log` holds everything.)

BIGQUERY / FILE EDITS:
- There is no `.md` log or archive to move entries between (retired) — the W5 outcome entry is written to `events.decision_log` via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)`.
- Apply mirroring edits directly to the kept factbase files `B_Sub_Pattern_Taxonomy.md`, `Watchlist.md`, `Operating_Protocols.md`; report the historical embedding-health trend only. D2a and the daily monitors own any live maintenance.

Write a brief `events.decision_log` entry (`CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)`) documenting the W5 cycle outcome: count of new entries processed, count of new sub-pattern instances extracted, factbase deltas if notable, any consistency-check anomalies surfaced.

If no entries qualify for sub-pattern extraction AND no factbase mirroring is needed: write the W5 outcome entry stating "No new entries to process and no factbase mirroring needed this cycle." and end without other file changes.

CHAT OUTPUT: one-line acknowledgment of factbase files edited (e.g., "events.decision_log W5-outcome written, B_Sub_Pattern_Taxonomy.md updated. 4 entries processed, 1 new B sub-pattern instance extracted.").

**`ops.web_calls` OBLIGATION (added 2026-08-24, fleet-wide alert-triage closure)** — unlike OPS1's fixed daily `^VIX` probe, W5 owes this row only conditionally: the MARKET-CALENDAR AUTO-EXTEND step's `mcp__FMP__marketHours` `holidays-by-exchange` pull (fires only when the calendar horizon drops under ~120 days) and the NO-GO COUNTERFACTUAL SHADOW-TRACKING sub-steps (a)/(b)'s `mcp__FMP__quote` fallback (fires only when IBKR's `search_contracts`/`get_price_snapshot` doesn't resolve a shadow ticker) are the sole metered surfaces in this routine's own text. A quiet cycle where neither fired legitimately owes zero rows, but any cycle where either one issued a call — including a failed or retried attempt — must write the batched `ops.web_calls` INSERT (`provider='fmp'`, one row per call) per the shared Run-logging template (§Observability, ~line 204-227) immediately before the terminal `sp_routine_end` call. This is restated here, per-routine, precisely because the two surfaces are conditional and easy to forget on a run where they happened to fire — the same reliability gap the OPS1 restatement above already closed for its own fixed call.

```
## M1a. Strategy-Blind Regime Scoring — deep research

Schedule: Monthly, before M1b.

```

This is a narrow, blinding-safe grant: it is a bare dated index-level series, carries no strategy, position or roster information, and the `^VIX`-only restriction is what keeps the rest of that table (park-menu tickers, SPY) out of a strategy-blind routine's view. Do NOT widen it to other tickers. For the M1a template specification read the strategy-blind slice `strategy/09_regime_scoring_strategy_blind_monthly.md` (the `## Regime scoring (strategy-blind, monthly)` section) — load that + `01_shared_regime_vocabulary.md` ONLY; do NOT load `02_regime_router`, `00_preamble`, or any strategy slice (blinding is now a hard file boundary — see the "Strategy reading" table + `ops/RUNBOOK.md` §9). Also read Experiment_Parameters.md, AI_Trading_Foundation.md.

CRITICAL BLINDING REQUIREMENT: This routine must NOT read Strategy.md sections describing individual strategies (Strategy A through Strategy E sections), per-strategy activation rules, or any document referencing strategy letters or mechanisms. M1a is strategy-blind by design. The output produced here feeds M1b (a separate routine) which then applies per-strategy mapping. If you find yourself referencing "Strategy A" or any strategy letter / mechanism in your reasoning, stop and re-scope — that work belongs in M1b, not here.

Produce strategy-blind regime scoring for every calendar month since M1a's last successful completion (normally the single prior calendar month; if one or more monthly cycles were missed, cover EACH missed month as its own labeled sub-period in PART 1, oldest first, in addition to the immediately-prior month — never silently skip a month's macro/regime coverage; owner directive 2026-07-25 CATCH-UP EVIDENCE WINDOW, see Observability § above). Two output files:

OUTPUT 1 — **write the structured macro indicators to `events.macro_series`** (one row per metric per release; the `Monthly_Macro_Data_*.md` audit file is RETIRED 2026-06-06 per Operating_Protocols §15 — do NOT recreate it). These are the audit trail of underlying inputs, NOT read by M1b. **Also append EVERY covered month's new prints to `events.macro_fred`** — the deep-history macro substrate that M5's `AI.FORECAST` reads — backfilling all missed months, not only the immediately-prior one, so M5 never inherits a silent forecast-substrate gap. **Pull via the FMP connector first** (`mcp__FMP__economics` `treasury-rates` + `economics-indicators`; map + YoY transforms in bigquery/07_fred_macro.sql §refresh), since the remote routine has FMP but may lack outbound `curl`; fall back to the FRED public CSV (no key) for any series FMP doesn't carry (notably `hy_oas`). Tag each row `source='FMP'` or `'FRED'`.

  **THE FIVE DAILY→MONTH-END METRICS NEED A PINNED DATE — never take "latest" for any of them (rule added 2026-08-05 after the defect below).** Most metrics here are monthly-native (CPI, PPI, payrolls, U-3, `fed_funds`, …) and cannot suffer this bug. Exactly five are DAILY series collapsed to a month-end level per `bigquery/07_fred_macro.sql:40-44` + line 76 ("the last VALID obs in the month, dated first-of-month") — **`vix`, `treasury_10y`, `treasury_2y`, `yield_curve_10y2y`, `hy_oas`** — and every one of them must be read for a SPECIFIC date: the covered month's **last trading day**. Resolve that date first, then:
  - **`vix`** — `SELECT close FROM state.signal_marks_curated WHERE ticker = '^VIX' AND mark_date = <that date>`. D2a STEP 1d ingests this daily and it is already correctly dated. Tag `source='FMP'`. Backfilling a missed month works the same way; the series carries ≥1y of history.
  - **`treasury_10y` / `treasury_2y`** — `mcp__FMP__economics` `treasury-rates` **with `from_date`/`to_date` both pinned to that date** (verified 2026-08-05: this endpoint returns explicitly dated rows, so it is safe *only* when you pass the date — an unpinned call returns the latest row and reintroduces the bug). Read `year10` / `year2`. Tag `source='FMP'`.
  - **`yield_curve_10y2y`** — the 10Y−2Y spread from the same pinned `treasury-rates` row, i.e. `.year10 − .year2` of the row you just read. **Be clear about what this does and does not verify (corrected 2026-08-06 — the rule as first written claimed a cross-check that was tautological).** Deriving the spread from the same row makes it consistent WITH those legs *by construction*: comparing it back to `treasury_10y − treasury_2y` is A−B against A−B and can never fail, so it provides ZERO verification. What actually guarantees this metric is correct is the DATE-PINNING of the `treasury-rates` call itself — that is the control, not any subsequent arithmetic check. **Optional genuine cross-check, when reachable:** FRED publishes `T10Y2Y` as an independent series (`bigquery/07_fred_macro.sql`); if you can read it for the same pinned date, comparing it to your derived spread IS a real two-source test — a disagreement means one of the two pulls is off-date, so stop and re-resolve. Note `fred.stlouisfed.org` returns HTTP 403 to a direct fetch and needs the Tavily-extract route with a cache-busting query param (see `hy_oas` above), so treat this as best-effort, never a gate. *(Historical note: the 2026-07 defect was exposed by exactly this kind of disagreement — the stored spread 0.47 was right while its own stored legs implied 0.45 — but that was only detectable because the spread had come from FRED's independent T10Y2Y print while the legs came from a stale FMP row. Same-row derivation would have hidden it.)*
  - **`hy_oas`** — FRED `BAMLH0A0HYM2` remains the only source (FMP does not carry it, `bigquery/07_fred_macro.sql:68`; no independent dated credit-spread series exists anywhere in this project). **Require the source to actually contain a row for that date.** If the print is not yet published, write NO `hy_oas` row for the month and backfill it on the next run — never substitute the nearest earlier date silently. **This series publishes with a ~1-day lag and updates around 08:52–11:30 CDT**, so a `first_trading_day` M1a run in the early-morning MT slot will routinely fire BEFORE the month-end print exists — expect the deferred-backfill path to be the NORMAL case here, not an exception. **Fetch note (measured 2026-08-05):** `fred.stlouisfed.org` returns **HTTP 403 to a direct `WebFetch`** (both the `fredgraph.csv` and `/data/*.txt` forms); the series page IS readable via Tavily extract, and a cache-busting query param (e.g. `?cb=<today>`) is needed or a stale crawl comes back. **Month-end nuance specific to this series:** FRED states *"when the last calendar day of the month takes place on the weekend, weekend observations will occur as a result of month ending accrued interest adjustments"* — so for `hy_oas` the month's last valid observation can legitimately be a **Saturday or Sunday date**, unlike the equity and treasury series. Take the last observation IN the month, not the last weekday.
  **Why this rule exists — do not revert it to an unpinned quote/CSV pull.** On 2026-08-03 M1a wrote July's `vix` as **17.09**, which is the **2026-07-30** close; the true 2026-07-31 close was **15.99**. It made the identical error on three more metrics in the same batch — **four of the five were wrong, and only `yield_curve_10y2y` (0.47) was right**: `treasury_10y` **4.68**, `treasury_2y` **4.23** and `hy_oas` **2.84** are all the 07-30 prints verbatim, against true 07-31 values of **4.75**, **4.28** and **2.85** (confirmed 2026-08-05 against date-pinned FMP `treasury-rates` and the FRED series page; all four corrected in `events.macro_fred` that day). That `yield_curve_10y2y` alone survived is the diagnostic worth remembering: its own FRED print had already published, so the stored spread was right while its own stored legs implied 0.45 — **an internally inconsistent set is the cheapest detector for this bug class.** Two independent causes, both structural, neither fixable by "try harder":
  (i) a live `quote` call has **no date argument at all** — it returns the latest close and physically cannot select a historical month-end; and
  (ii) the FRED `VIXCLS` CSV publishes with a lag, and M1a's cadence is `monthly first_trading_day` (`ops/cadence.yaml`), so it fires exactly when the just-closed month's final print is least likely to be posted. This is a **recurring monthly collision**, not a one-off — the same run corrected June to 16.45 (which matches the 06-30 close exactly), so the failure is specifically "the newest print isn't there yet," not a bad transform.
  Consequences that actually landed, as the reason to keep this pinned: the wrong value propagated into `analytics.deployed_twr_forecast` (2026-08-03 vintage, vix path 16.91→17.45→17.58) and produced a **false** "Above band: `vix` 17.09 (+0.41)" calibration breach in M5's `forecast-monitor` `events.decision_log` entry — the true 15.99 sits inside the July vintage's 80% band [13.28, 16.68]. The trading router was never affected (it reads `TECHNICAL_SIGNAL/VIX_REGIME`, computed by D2a from the same dated ingest), which is exactly why routing M1a to that ingest closes the gap. This keeps the macro forecast current without depending on agent-side HTTP. `macro_fred` is a separate bulk/forecast substrate, distinct from this hand-curated `macro_series` audit table:

PART 1 — Coverage of every calendar month since M1a's last successful completion (normally just the prior month; label each covered month explicitly, oldest first). If a section has no material items for a given month, state so.

Section 1 — Macro data releases from the prior calendar month
Per indicator: latest value, release date, prior release, trailing 3-month trend.
- CPI headline and core (YoY, MoM)

Global trade, oil/commodities, sovereign credit, or global risk sentiment. Per event: what happened, source, observable market reaction.

Section 6 — Cross-asset and risk-sentiment indicators (compensatory)

Close PART 1 with a 3–5 sentence summary of the month's character — strategy-blind language only.

OUTPUT 2 — **write the 5-axis regime scores to `events.regime_events` (scope `FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS`)**: one row per axis (growth_momentum / inflation_trend / policy_stance / risk_sentiment / shock_overlay) + the `_integrative` row, each with its categorical value + brief rationale (+ a `fallback_suppression` flag row when applicable). **Score ONLY the most-recently-completed covered month here — never one row per covered month.** M1b/the router read only the LATEST `events.regime_events` row, so on a multi-month catch-up the earlier missed month(s) surfaced in PART 1 are backward context/trend color only; this OUTPUT 2 5-axis score stays a single current snapshot, exactly as today. ```

Within each, identify pairs where:
- Both have market cap and 30-day ADV sufficient for E execution (flag pairs requiring ETF substitution at small portfolio sizes) — unchanged mechanical floor
- Trailing 252-day daily-return correlation ≥ 0.3 (the §19 Layer-1 population band). Pairs at corr ≥ 0.5 meet E's SPEC FLOOR — that number derives from E's frozen Entry criterion 3 (`strategy/07_strategy_e.md`, §19's spec-floor rail), not from a screen tune — and are the only pairs eligible to advance to PART 2. Pairs in the 0.3–0.49 band are `below_spec_floor` context only (max 3 recorded per call — a cap distinct from §19's sub-net escape valve, bounding BOTH the Monthly_E_Pairs.md PART 1 rows and the fields-JSON items, which must list the same pairs): interesting co-movers logged as SL1 ideation evidence per §19, NEVER advanced as E pair candidates
- Both have reported earnings or filed 10-Q/10-K within the last 90 days — unchanged mechanical freshness gate
Log ONE `entry_type='research-screen'` decision_log row (screen='pair-divergence') per §19's logging contract — including quiet months (`surfaced_count=0`, empty arrays; `legacy_rule_pass` = corr ≥ 0.5, record-only benchmark).

Per pair: provisional L and S (refined in PART 2), industry group, 252-day correlation, most recent earnings/filing dates, approximate short borrow rate per leg if estimable, individual-stock vs. ETF-substitution execution flag. Table organized by industry group.

PART 2 — Ranked shortlist. The downstream M4 routine reads this PART 2 verbatim and schedules pair-thesis-construction events, so rank explicitly with priority tier.

Per pair, preliminary narrative-divergence assessment strictly from public sources: 10-K/10-Q, 8-K, earnings transcripts, public analyst reports (full text), press releases, public news, public industry data. No expert networks, management access, conference-private context, buy-side intelligence, industry contacts, or channel checks. If analysis requires such sources, abandon and note why.

Rank shortlist of up to 10 pair candidates. Per pair:
(a) L (laggard, long) and S (leader, short) designation with public-document reasoning
(b) Narrative divergence thesis
(c) Reconvergence indicator(s): specific future public events or disclosures marking thesis playing out
(d) Estimated short borrow cost and whether it fits ≤ 15% of expected thesis return per Strategy.md
(e) Individual-stock vs. ETF substitution execution path
(f) Priority tier (top-3 / rest)

Exclude pairs where either leg is in the open E book.

This is the general rule from Observability § above, restated here because it is the one call in this routine that must never be skipped (a 2026-07-09 audit found an analogous D2 session skip this exact call for its own dependency, so it is now inlined per-routine rather than left to a shared preamble alone).

**TRADING-ENABLE GATE — A STAGING GATE, NOT A ROUTINE GATE (self-improvement audit B-1-obs, 2026-07-03; blast-radius fix 2026-07-27, `INCIDENT[ref=423ecc02-fdb7-4f47-9445-d8c79d399e8c]`).** `CALL ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts()` (best-effort), then read the gate NON-FATALLY: `SELECT trading_enabled, halt_reason FROM state.trading_enabled`. If FALSE, `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('critical', 'M4', 'trading_halted', 'Order staging blocked: trading is HALTED. See payload for the triggering routine and reason.', TO_JSON_STRING(STRUCT('M4' AS routine, <halt_reason> AS halt_reason)))`, carry the verdict forward as a session fact, and **CONTINUE** — do NOT abort. A FALSE verdict blocks EVERY order-craft point in this routine — enumerated here so none is missed: section C's confirmed-exit craft AND section H's 30-trade-gate TERMINATION-CLOSE craft (which executes "the close + deterministic redistribution per the D2 termination procedure" and is just as much an order craft as the exit). Each carries its own inline **TRADING-ENABLE RE-CHECK** below: decline to craft, write no `ORDER_STAGED` row, and record the decision as staged-but-halted via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` citing `halt_reason`. That list is a reading aid, NOT the definition — the rule is "any order craft", so a craft site added later is covered whether or not anyone updates it. It does NOT block the research reads, the A-queue/D-re-screen/E-pair `PENDING_ANALYSIS` enqueues, the 30-trade-gate EVALUATION itself (only the resulting close-craft), Watchlist.md updates, or run logging — those stage nothing, and a halt that silently swallows a month's research enqueues starves D2 of the very queue it exists to drain. ROUTER ACTIVATION FLIPS FROM M1b — for each strategy with FLIP TO ACTIVATE or FLIP TO DO-NOT-ACTIVATE (the strategy set is whatever M1b emitted, enumerated from `state.strategy_roster` — a newly roster-active newcomer receives flips automatically, so no A-E list is hardcoded here; rev 2026-07-10 — Strategy Arsenal autonomy conversion):

No cap — drain the entire A-queue. D2 runs them.
     * Remove processed names from Watchlist.md A-queue (or mark "queued <date>").
   - **A FLIP TO DO-NOT-ACTIVATE for any strategy — halt new-position activity.** Supersede any pending `PENDING_ANALYSIS` thesis-construction entries for that strategy (insert a `superseded` status row to `events.queue_events`). Existing positions are unaffected (per Strategy.md exit rules — DO-NOT-ACTIVATE blocks new entries, not existing-position management).

Per Experiment_Parameters.md "Kill criteria (per-strategy)" + the success threshold:
   - **30-trade gate:** **PRECONDITION FIXED (self-improvement audit 2026-07-15, CONFIRMED GAP probe-stake-floor-prose-only) — for each strategy whose `state.strategy_roster.current_state = 'PROBE'` AND whose latest `perf.kill_flags.gate_reached = TRUE`** (verified live 2026-07-15: `perf.strategy_daily` has NO `gate_status` column — the prior instruction text named a column that has never existed; `gate_reached = (closed_trades >= 30)` is the real, live signal, computed in `perf.kill_flags`/`bigquery/03_twr_engine.sql`. Gating on `current_state = 'PROBE'` ALSO gives this bullet its own idempotency for free — `gate_reached` itself is stateless and stays TRUE forever once tripped, but a strategy leaves the PROBE state the moment either branch below resolves, so it naturally drops out of this precondition on every subsequent D2 run): read the maintained **deployed unit value** and **SGOV index** at the 30-trade mark; nominal excess = `deployed_unit_value ÷ sgov_index − 1`; apply the **post-tax** haircut (short-term cap-gains rate per Experiment_Parameters.md on the realized-gain portion) and **post-inflation** haircut (CPI over the first-trade-to-gate span) → **excess real return**. **WASH-SALE ADJUSTMENT (self-improvement audit 2026-07-15, CONFIRMED GAP wash-sale-loss-not-in-gate-math) — fold in BEFORE applying the post-tax haircut:** `SELECT SUM(estimated_disallowed_loss) FROM state.wash_sale_exposure WHERE close_strategy = <strategy>` (`bigquery/41_tax_lots.sql` — built specifically because "a disallowed loss reduces the actual post-tax figure below what the naive TWR-minus-tax-rate estimate implies," Experiment_Parameters.md, but nothing had ever read it downstream). A disallowed loss is not currently deductible, so it must be ADDED BACK to the taxable realized-gain base the post-tax haircut applies to (the opposite of subtracting it) before clamping the taxable base at 0 — this makes the post-tax haircut slightly MORE conservative (a strategy with real wash-sale exposure clears the gate on a smaller true after-tax excess than the naive figure suggested), never less. **If < 0% → terminate** — **TRADING-ENABLE RE-CHECK (2026-07-27, `INCIDENT[ref=423ecc02-fdb7-4f47-9445-d8c79d399e8c]`) — apply BEFORE crafting:** if the `state.trading_enabled` verdict carried forward from this routine's TRADING-ENABLE GATE reads FALSE, do NOT craft and do NOT write an `ORDER_STAGED` row — record the decision as staged-but-halted via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` citing `halt_reason`, and continue to the next item. This is deliberately restated here rather than left to the gate paragraph alone: the pre-2026-07-27 design enforced the halt by aborting the routine, so the craft sites never needed their own check; now they do. (execute the close + deterministic redistribution per the D2 termination procedure / Experiment_Parameters.md "Strategy termination and capital redistribution"); write the gate post-mortem to `events.decision_log` (`CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)`). **If ≥ 0% → mark the gate CLEARED**: **write an ADOPTED `events.strategy_lifecycle` row (driver_routine='D2')** — self-improvement audit 2026-07-15, CONFIRMED GAP probe-stake-floor-prose-only: this transition was previously NEVER WRITTEN by anything, so a strategy that cleared its gate stayed in `current_state = 'PROBE'` forever (harmless to `state.active_strategy_codes`/`is_active`, which already includes PROBE, but semantically wrong and, before this same session's `analytics.strategy_nav` fix, silently invisible to NAV/sizing) — plus an `events.regime_events` (`STRATEGY_ACTIVATION`, unchanged, still active) update and an `events.decision_log` entry (permission to continue; not a success verdict). **THEN RAISE THE GRADUATION NOTICE (2026-08-04, owner directive "notify me by email on every roster add/drop"): `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','M4','strategy_graduated', '<code> (<name>) CLEARED the 30-trade gate and graduated PROBE -> ADOPTED — real excess after tax and inflation <X.X>%. Now sized as a full roster member.', '<JSON per the preamble ROSTER-CHANGE NOTICE contract; reason = the measured post-tax/post-inflation excess>')`** — this transition previously raised NOTHING at all, so the single moment an autonomously-adopted strategy proved itself and moved to full sizing was the one roster event with no operator-facing signal whatsoever (it is also the transition the `strategy_adopted` category misleadingly appeared to name; that category has been renamed `strategy_probe_registered` at its real site in SL5). Raise it only on the CLEARED branch — the `< 0%` branch terminates, and that path already notifies via `termination_close_staged` plus SL5's `strategy_deregistered`. Record the evaluation either way. (Strategy D's gate is expected never to be reached — low turnover; documented and fine.)
   - **Mark-to-market underperformance (#4):** for each strategy whose `perf.strategy_daily` row shows **`deployed_days` ≥ ~756 (≈ 36 months active)**, compute the rolling-12-month deployed-vs-SGOV gap from the `perf.strategy_daily` series — `(deployed_unit_value/sgov_index now) ÷ (deployed_unit_value/sgov_index ~12 months ago) − 1`; if it has trailed SGOV by **≥ 10 percentage points over any rolling 12-month window** (router-deactivation periods already excluded, since the indices only advance on deployed days), enqueue a `PENDING_REVIEW` entry (`INSERT INTO events.queue_events`, queue='PENDING_REVIEW'; review_type m2m-termination; the strategy; trigger_context = the measured 36-month-active + rolling-12-month gap; attacker_due_date next trading day; orchestrator_due_date +1; status pending). The Attacker/Orchestrator adjudicate; on TERMINATE they execute termination + redistribution inline. (At ~6 weeks of experiment age this cannot fire until ~2029 — a no-op until then.)

DEFERRAL DISCIPLINE: deferrals don't chain. Specify trigger and conservative-default fallback for any deferred decision. Enqueue deferred analyses to the `PENDING_ANALYSIS` queue (`events.queue_events`; never the calendar).

CALENDAR MCP USAGE: Claude calls the Calendar MCP directly only for a non-craftable order's manual-entry `[Claude] Confirm order` event (D exits in section C; strategy-termination closes in section H; 2026-07-09 — craftable orders rely on IBKR's own notification instead). Time zone per Experiment_Parameters.md.

CHAT OUTPUT:
- Exit order(s) as crafted instructions (tap-to-confirm deep link + `SIDE QTY TICKER TYPE LIMIT TIF` summary) grouped by execution day (or "no order").
- One-line acknowledgment of file edits, `PENDING_ANALYSIS` queue entries enqueued, and confirm-order events created.

If no orders, no file changes, no queue entries: "No actions required."
```

## M5. Deployed-TWR & Macro Forecast — regular routine

Runs monthly, after M4 (Monthly Action Conversion). The forward-looking monitoring overlay: a zero-shot `AI.FORECAST` (BigQuery built-in TimesFM — **no model to train or host**) over the deployed-TWR engine and, once it accrues enough history, the macro series. **Advisory / early-warning ONLY — it never stages an exit, termination, or activation change. Kill/gate triggers fire on REALISED values (`perf.kill_flags`), never on a forecast** (Experiment_Parameters.md kill-criteria discipline). Not deep research; pure BigQuery. DDL + query templates: `bigquery/06_forecast.sql`.

```
Read access scope: Monthly cadence, BigQuery read + write. Read `perf.strategy_daily` (the deployed-TWR series), `perf.kill_flags`, `events.macro_series`, and the prior run's `analytics.deployed_twr_forecast`. No web research or repo factbase reads required.

**SAME-DAY DOUBLE-RUN GUARD (completeness-critic N-4, 2026-07-16 — see the shared Observability section's generalized guard)** — FIRST, before the dependency gate below, before anything else: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ops.run_log WHERE routine='M5' AND run_date=<today, America/Denver> AND status='completed'`; if `>= 1`, output "M5 already completed today (a prior fire — OPS0 catch-up or M5's own scheduled trigger — already completed; this is the expected redundant re-invocation, not an error)." and END IMMEDIATELY — do NOT re-run the forecast, do NOT log another `started`/`completed` row.

**DEPENDENCY GATE — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap — `CALL ops.sp_assert_deps('M5', ['M4'], <today>)` BEFORE the start-log, before anything else in this routine.** Aborts (RAISE) + raises a `missing_dependency` critical if M4 has no `completed` run anywhere in the current monthly period — M4 is `monthly_ftd`, so since `bigquery/114_period_aware_dependency_gate.sql` (2026-07-29) the gate is satisfied by any M4 completion with `run_date BETWEEN DATE_TRUNC(in_run_date, MONTH) AND in_run_date`, not only a completion on this exact calendar day; self-bootstrapping. This is the general rule from Observability § above, restated here because it is the one call in this routine that must never be skipped (a 2026-07-09 audit found an analogous D2 session skip this exact call for its own dependency, so it is now inlined per-routine rather than left to a shared preamble alone).

STEP 0 — ensure the store + early-warning view exist: idempotently run `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS analytics.deployed_twr_forecast` **and** `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW analytics.twr_forecast_vs_actual` (bigquery/06_forecast.sql §store + §B). The view reads the table + `perf.strategy_daily`, so it is safe to (re)create even when the table is empty — STEP 1 needs it to exist on the next run.

STEP 1 — FORECAST-VS-ACTUAL early-warning (skip on the first-ever run). Query `analytics.twr_forecast_vs_actual` (the most-recent PRIOR run's `deployed_unit_value` forecast vs realised `perf.strategy_daily` for now-elapsed dates). Flag any strategy whose realised deployed-unit-value landed BELOW the prior forecast's `pi_lower` (downside surprise — possible regime shift / unmodeled deterioration) or above `pi_upper`. This is the calibration + early-warning signal.

Also read `analytics.excess_forecast_vs_actual` (the m2m-proxy series, previously stored-but-never-calibrated) and `analytics.macro_forecast_vs_actual` (last vintage's macro forecasts vs since-published FRED prints; bigquery/77_forecast_consumption.sql), folding notable breaches into the STEP 5 entry. ALERT DISCIPLINE (strategy series only; macro breaches stay decision_log-only): restrict to the MOST RECENT prior vintage — `forecast_run_date = (SELECT MAX(run_date) FROM analytics.deployed_twr_forecast WHERE run_date < CURRENT_DATE("America/Denver"))` — never alert off older vintages. First heal: `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved=TRUE, resolved_ts=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note="band breach healed (M5 STEP 1)" WHERE NOT resolved AND source="M5" AND category="forecast_downside_breach"` for each open breach alert whose strategy/series shows no below_band row in the latest vintage (sanctioned in-place resolution — the bigquery/34 lifecycle pattern; ops.alerts is not append-only-watched). Then for each strategy whose realised `deployed_unit_value` OR `excess_vs_sgov` landed below the latest prior vintage's `pi_lower`: `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once("warning","M5","forecast_downside_breach","<strategy> — realised <series> below the prior 90% pi_lower (downside surprise; advisory, never a trigger)","<JSON: strategy, series, forecast_run_date, forecast_date, pi_lower, actual>")` so the early warning reaches the monitored email channel (alert_emailer.gs already emails severity=warning). Keep the message string exactly as templated — sp_raise_alert_once dedups on unresolved (category, message).

STEP 2 — NEW deployed-TWR forecast. Run `AI.FORECAST` per active strategy over `perf.strategy_daily`, horizon 21 (~one trading month), `confidence_level => 0.9`, for two series: `deployed_unit_value` (drawdown / profitability path) and `excess_vs_sgov` (relative-perf / mark-to-market path). INSERT every forecast row into `analytics.deployed_twr_forecast` with `run_date = CURRENT_DATE('America/Denver')` (bigquery/06_forecast.sql §A — INSERT only rows whose `ai_forecast_status` is empty, so a newly-activated strategy with too few deployed days is skipped rather than written as NaN). (29 deployed days at 2026-06 is enough to run — AI.FORECAST handles the business-day spacing; intervals are wide now and tighten as history accrues.)

STEP 3 — KILL/GATE TRAJECTORY check (advisory). From the new forecast, note whether the central path or `pi_lower` of `deployed_unit_value` trends toward a kill threshold over the horizon — drawdown-kill `deployed_unit_value / peak_unit_value − 1 ≤ −0.50` (#1), or `excess_vs_sgov ≤ −0.10` (the mark-to-market #4 proxy, which only becomes a live trigger at `deployed_days ≥ 756`). A heads-up for the next M4 gate/kill review — NOT a trigger. Do NOT stage any exit or termination off the forecast.

STEP 4 — MACRO forecast (FRED-backed, un-gated). Run `AI.FORECAST` over `state.macro_fred_latest` (15 FRED-derived monthly regime metrics with deep history — 37–54 months each; St. Louis Fed public CSV, no API key; bigquery/07_fred_macro.sql): `data_col => 'value'`, `timestamp_col => 'ref_month'`, `id_cols => ['metric']`, horizon 3, `confidence_level => 0.8`. INSERT the rows whose `ai_forecast_status` is empty into `analytics.deployed_twr_forecast` (`series` = metric, `entity` = 'macro'). The ≥8-obs gate is satisfied for all seeded metrics — keep it only as a guard for any thin/new metric (skip + record `insufficient history (n=<k>)`). Advisory only; TimesFM zero-shot short-horizon central paths on policy-driven series (e.g. `fed_funds`) are noisy, so weight the trend + interval over the point. `macro_fred` is refreshed monthly by M1a appending the new prints (bigquery/07_fred_macro.sql §refresh); M5 forecasts off whatever is current. (The M1a-curated `events.macro_series` audit table is separate and not used here.)

STEP 5 — write a brief decision entry via **`CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)`** (`entry_type='forecast-monitor'`; appends to `events.decision_log` + embeds in one call, per Operating_Protocols §15): per-strategy horizon-end forecast + interval for `deployed_unit_value` and `excess_vs_sgov`; any STEP 1 band breaches; the STEP 3 trajectory note; macro coverage (metrics forecasted vs. gated).

CHAT OUTPUT: one line — e.g. "M5 forecast: B duv(21d) 0.999 [0.97,1.02], excess −0.4% [−2.1%,+1.3%]; D duv 0.96 [0.92,1.00]; no prior-band breach; no kill-trajectory flag; macro 0/12 (insufficient history). Wrote 84 forecast rows + 1 decision_log entry."
