## SL2. Strategy Draft, Revise & Post-mortem — regular routine

Queue-driven (fires Sun-Thu; no-ops unless a `PENDING_DRAFT` item is due). The dedicated autonomous EDITORIAL routine of the lifecycle — it authors a QUALIFYING candidate's full mechanism section + self-contained pre-mortem, redrafts on an AR_orc REVISION REQUIRED verdict, and authors termination post-mortems. It OVERTURNS the retired "pre-mortem revision is out of scope for a routine / the participant revises" carve-out. Runs with INDEPENDENT context from SL1 and the AR reviewers (multi-scrutiny independence). Never stages orders, never touches capital, never edits the live roster (SL5 does).

```
Read access scope: daily (queue-driven), with Strategy.md WRITE permission in the CANDIDATE namespace and, only for a `strategy-revise` task explicitly scoped to a live pre-mortem, the named strategy's section of `strategy/08_pre_mortems.md`. Read the draft queue `events.queue_events` / `state.open_queue_detail` (queue `PENDING_DRAFT`), `state.strategy_candidates`, `state.adversarial_reviews_current` (for a revise task's attacker/orchestrator output), `strategy/roster.yaml`, `Strategy.md`, `AI_Trading_Foundation.md`, `ops.arsenal_control`, `state.active_playbook` (strategy_playbook loop deltas — empty until that loop's gate clears). WRITE `events.premortem_flags` / `events.premortem_flag_outcomes` (`bigquery/42_adversarial_flag_hit.sql`, ITEM 22) — append-only, per (A)/(B)/(C) below.

Observability: connector pre-flight, `ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts()`, run-logging, failure alerts — per the shared Observability section; do not restate. Queue-driven, so (per the queue_driven monitoring rule) it is monitored via `state.stalled_runs` + `ops/triggers.json`, NOT `cadence_watch`/`period_watch`.

**ARSENAL KILL-SWITCH GATE — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap — `CALL ops.sp_assert_arsenal_enabled('SL2')` before anything else.** RAISEs + `critical` alert (abort) if the arsenal loop is disabled/frozen.

Scan `PENDING_DRAFT` for the oldest due item and dispatch by `item_type` (process all due items this fire, each as an isolated sub-task for fresh context where available). If none: run the CLOSE YOUR OWN PRIOR NOTICES step below FIRST (it binds every fire, including this one), then chat output "No strategy-draft/revise/post-mortem tasks due." and exit.

**`PENDING_DRAFT` LANE CONTRACT — binds EVERY producer that enqueues into this lane; pinned 2026-08-18. Producers do not restate it, they cite it.** `PENDING_ANALYSIS` and `PENDING_REVIEW` each carry one document-wide schema paragraph that every producer inherits automatically (the `state.trading_day_today` due-date rule in the preamble Calendar section; the review-queue block in the Adversarial Review section). `PENDING_DRAFT` never had one — its conventions were retrofitted per-producer, one site at a time, only as each gap was discovered. That structural absence, not any one routine's carelessness, is why the same defect shape has now recurred three times in three days: the AR_orc→SL2 `due_date` offset that was unstated here, drifted on 2026-08-16 and cost two SL2 fires as no-ops (fixed d66da71); the SL3→SL5 `PENDING_ROSTER` handoff that named no `queue` and no `item_key` on either side, both NOT NULL with no default (found 2026-08-18 before its first firing, fixed 6467b4d); and route (C) below, whose two enqueue sites — D2 §5's DRAWDOWN/foundation/m2m termination handler and AR_orc's m2m-termination verdict — still name no `item_key` and no `due_date` at all. Route (C) has never fired (`events.queue_events` holds zero `item_type='post-mortem'` rows), so this is closed before its first use, exactly like the SL3→SL5 case: the failure mode of an unpinned lane is not a loud error, it is two sessions with no shared memory each inventing a value and the consumer silently never finding the producer's row, with both `ops.run_log` rows reading `completed`.

Every `PENDING_DRAFT` enqueue writes at minimum:

```
queue      = 'PENDING_DRAFT'                 -- NOT NULL, no default
item_key   = per item_type below             -- NOT NULL, no default; STABLE across cycles
item_type  = 'strategy-draft' | 'strategy-revise' | 'post-mortem'
status     = 'pending'                       -- NOT NULL, no default; SL2 writes 'complete' on drain
strategy   = the strategy or candidate code (A-E, or a candidate code)
due_date   = the NEXT calendar day after `state.trading_day_today.today` (America/Denver)
```

- **`due_date` — the next Denver calendar day after `state.trading_day_today.today`, never the next TRADING day and never a hand-computed date.** SL2 fires Sun-Thu and drains `due_date <= today`, so a next-calendar-day offset is always reachable on the following fire; a next-*trading*-day offset silently skips the item across a weekend, which is the 2026-08-16 drift. Per the preamble's timezone rule, `today` comes from `state.trading_day_today` — never the assistant-context `currentDate` (UTC-based; already rolled over during evening MT) and never local Bash `date`.
- **`item_key` — stable per item_type, and the cycle number NEVER belongs in the key** (it goes in `payload.cycle_number`, so a re-enqueue of the same work is recognisable as the same work):
  - `strategy-draft` (from SL1 STEP 4) → `draft-<CODE>`
  - `strategy-revise` (from AR_orc Step 4) → `revise-premortem-<CODE>-<review suffix>`
  - `post-mortem` (from D2 §5 / AR_orc) → `postmortem-<CODE>-<retired_date YYYY-MM-DD>`
- **`payload.review_type`** is carried on `strategy-revise` (`'pre-mortem'` for a live-strategy pre-mortem task, `'strategy-adoption'` for a candidate task) — it is what route (B) dispatches on.
- **`trigger_context` is NOT a column of `events.queue_events`.** The column list is `event_id, event_ts, queue, item_key, item_type, status, strategy, ticker, due_date, conservative_default, artifact_path, payload, note`. Every site in this document that reads "`trigger_context=<x>`" means **`payload.trigger_context`** — writing it as a bare column is an immediate error, not a silent miss, but the prose has said it at four sites and is corrected here once rather than at each.

(A) **strategy-draft** (from SL1). For the QUALIFYING candidate in `trigger_context`, and only while the concurrent-incubation cap is still open:
   1. Author a `## Strategy <code> [CANDIDATE]` section in Strategy.md (candidate namespace — NOT roster-active) mirroring the A-E structure: Thesis with each rule inline-cited to a foundation edge/disadvantage; Differentiation vs the live roster; numbered Entry criteria; Exit / invalidation rules; declared frequency; a fresh per-thesis Capital-at-Risk budget with no numeric ceiling, justified against the seven-factor list in `Experiment_Parameters.md` rev 19 §Position size and adversarially attacked on size; classical-method delegation list; exactly one Boolean router-activation line + the M1b fundamental-analysis question for it; kill-criteria structure. Also SELECT playbook_key, delta_text FROM state.active_playbook and honor any delta addressed to the candidate's archetype/sub-pattern, citing the playbook_key in the draft (empty today — the strategy_playbook loop's output surface; loop-completeness audit 2026-07-16: without this read, a cleared playbook delta would change nothing anywhere).
   1b. **JUDGMENT-NATIVE MACHINERY (owner-approved Redesign B, 2026-07-19 — `AI_DECISION_REDESIGN.md` §3).** The candidate's entry/exit machinery MAY be authored as a structured judgment protocol — criteria the executing session evaluates fresh each time, with declared conviction gates and explicit invalidation criteria — instead of fixed numeric triggers, and SHOULD be where the cited edge is judgment-shaped (SL1 STEP 2's preference). Four REQUIREMENTS, none waivable: (a) the protocol must define unambiguously what constitutes a signal event AND declare its expected signal-rate band exactly like a numeric spec — SHADOW's `state.strategy_shadow_readiness` signal-rate gate needs countable signals, and a protocol whose signals can't be counted fails qualification at SL1 (c); (b) the fresh, seven-factor-justified per-thesis CaR budget (with no numeric ceiling), the mandatory adversarial attack on size, every kill trigger, the 30-trade gate, and every graduation rail apply UNCHANGED — judgment-native machinery changes what the spec says, never which rails bind it; (c) spec-freeze applies identically — the protocol TEXT freezes at SHADOW entry (`spec_hash` covers prose exactly as it covers formulas; any later wording change = terminate-and-restart-as-new); (d) the pre-mortem attacks the protocol like any machinery — including the failure mode unique to this class, criteria drift under loss pressure, which the pre-mortem must address explicitly.
   2. Author a self-contained 7-section pre-mortem artifact for the candidate (Experiment_Parameters.md pre-mortem format + self-containment requirement, so the strict-blinded attacker can review it standalone).
   2b. **REGISTER PRE-MORTEM FLAGS (self-improvement audit ITEM 22, 2026-07-11).** For every Tier 1/2/3 flag the pre-mortem carries forward with a named review-trigger condition (the flags AR_att/AR_orc accept rather than reject the draft over), `INSERT INTO events.premortem_flags` (`strategy_code`, `review_id = NULL` — the correlated `strategy-adoption` review id is not yet assigned at authoring time and is not required for scoring, which reads by `strategy_code`, `tier`, `flag_text`, `review_trigger_text`, `backfilled = FALSE`). This is the pre-registration `analytics.adversarial_flag_hit` (`bigquery/42_adversarial_flag_hit.sql`) measures against at termination — never skip it even for a flag that looks minor.
   3. Derive ALL parameters FRESH and write `state.strategy_candidates.derivation_provenance` (JSON: each parameter, its derivation, source) — the anti-inheritance evidence SL1/AR check.
   4. Regenerate the candidate slice via `scripts/split_strategy.py` (stable code-keyed numbering — the fixed tail never renumbers).
   5. Enqueue an `events.queue_events` `PENDING_REVIEW` `review_type='strategy-adoption'` (`conservative_default='REJECT'`, `cycle_number=1`, `artifact_path` = the candidate pre-mortem) and write an AUTHORING→UNDER_REVIEW `events.strategy_lifecycle` row.

(B) **strategy-revise** (from an AR_orc REVISION REQUIRED verdict). Read the orchestrator output for the flagged Tier-1 defects. For a candidate task, redraft ONLY those defects; re-derive any changed parameter FRESH and diff-check it against the prior draft AND any `is_restart_of` source to block inheritance; `cycle_number++`; re-enqueue the `strategy-adoption` review. For a live-strategy pre-mortem task, identified by `review_type='pre-mortem'`, an active strategy code, and `artifact_path='strategy/08_pre_mortems.md'`, revise ONLY that strategy's named pre-mortem section and re-enqueue the same `pre-mortem` review. **`payload.artifact_source_commit` on that re-enqueued row is a FULL 40-character SHA, resolved AFTER the revision commit lands via `git log -1 --format=%H -- <artifact_path>` — PINNED 2026-08-18 by AR_orc, previously unstated anywhere in this document (a repo-wide grep for the field name returned zero specifications).** It drifted the moment it was left unstated: SL2's 2026-08-17 fire re-enqueued `premortem-C-2026-a3` cycle 14 and `premortem-E-2026-a3` cycle 10 in one write (`event_ts` 2026-08-18T01:37:58Z) carrying `artifact_source_commit='d66da712'` — an 8-character value that resolves to no git object at all, where the artifact's real head was `d66da71085fb2617366a99bedd1b30bce6b04706`. Every other value ever written to this field, across every prior SL2/AR_orc batch, is a full 40-char SHA, so this was one data-entry error rather than a code defect — but nothing mechanical catches it: `events.queue_events.payload` is free-form JSON with no schema validation, unlike `ops.sp_write_adversarial_review`'s `p_source_commit_sha`, which hard-ASSERTs `^[0-9a-f]{40}([0-9a-f]{24})?$` (`bigquery/145_adversarial_review_writer_serialization.sql`:74-76) and would have rejected the same literal outright. **It cost nothing that cycle only because AR_orc's Step 1.5 artifact-version gate reads the ATTACKER TRANSCRIPT's ASSERT-validated `source_commit_sha`, never this payload field — keep it that way.** This field is provenance/audit trail, never a gate input. Do not confuse it with the sibling `payload.git_commit`, which by established convention carries the SHORT hash; the two are not interchangeable, which is precisely why Step 1.5 warns that comparing a short SHA against a full one is a guaranteed false mismatch. **WRITE-SITE VERIFICATION — MANDATORY, added 2026-08-18 by SL2, the routine that owns this write.** The pin above states the CONTRACT but specifies no check, and the contract alone is exactly what already failed: `d66da712` is not a truncation of `d66da71085fb2617366a99bedd1b30bce6b04706` — its eighth character differs — so the value was hand-typed from a glance at a short hash rather than shortened from a correct one, and re-reading the same prose would not have caught it. So CAPTURE the command's output into the payload instead of transcribing a hash read off a log line or a commit summary, and VERIFY before the INSERT: the value must be 40 lowercase hex characters AND `git cat-file -t <sha>` must return `commit`. One local git call, no network, no BigQuery cost. It is the ONLY guard this field has — `events.queue_events.payload` is unvalidated free-form JSON, so unlike `ops.sp_write_adversarial_review`'s `p_source_commit_sha` regex ASSERT there is no write-time rejection anywhere downstream, and a bad value that lands is durable. A detector view over already-landed payloads was considered here and deliberately NOT built: this is the field's only origination site, so a guard AT the writer prevents the class outright where a detector could only report it after the fact, and adding live SQL for it would multiply machinery for a field that by the pin above is provenance-only and gates nothing. **THE 2026-08-17 VALUES WERE ALREADY REPAIRED IN BAND — do NOT write a correction row for them.** Read the pin above as history, not as a live defect. AR_att's 2026-08-18 fire consumed both `pending` rows and carried the field forward CORRECTED on its own `attacker-complete` rows — `premortem-C-2026-a3` cycle 14 (`event_id` `6c8b2386-b8bd-40b2-8a00-690b9d5b8253`) and `premortem-E-2026-a3` cycle 10 (`event_id` `a0ca0390-ffbf-4f15-a690-bb047fac5a0b`), each carrying `artifact_source_commit='d66da71085fb2617366a99bedd1b30bce6b04706'` plus a `payload.enqueue_payload_commit_note` recording what the consumed row had said and why it was wrong. A repo-wide search establishes the negative: **no document anywhere states the rule** — not this file, not `task_plan/SL2.md`/`AR_att.md`/`AR_orc.md`, not `Experiment_Parameters.md`'s pre-mortem-format section, not `Operating_Protocols.md`, not `strategy/08_pre_mortems.md`'s own preamble, not `strategy/roster.yaml` — and **nothing mechanical guards it**: no script, CI check, dbt test or SQL object parses or asserts on the literal `**Revision:**` string (`scripts/check_roster_consistency.py` segments this very file per strategy and never looks at it), while the artifact-version machinery keys on the **SHA256 of the section text** and `cycle_number` keys on `events.adversarial_reviews`. The marker is therefore unguarded free text that only a routine's own discipline keeps correct — the same standing as `payload.artifact_source_commit` above, and it earns the same write-site rule.

The reason it was never written down is that until recently the question had no content: rev and cycle were the same integer on **every** revision SL2 has ever written, and SL2's own record says both in one breath at every site — `events.decision_log` "Revised to rev 9 … re-enqueued for cycle 9" (D; B at 11, C at 13, E at 9, all 2026-08-13), "Revised to rev 10 … cycle 10" (E) and "rev 14 … cycle 14" (C, 2026-08-17), and `ops.alerts` "C rev 14 (cycle 14), E rev 10 (cycle 10)". So the identity was broken once, recorded in prose inside the artifact, and never promoted to a rule.
- **Revision advances outside the loop entirely.** An owner-directive commit can rewrite a section with no SL2 fire: `60878d6d558dbf7b68ec5392edf3d4d57ae3e19b` (2026-08-18) took Strategy E from rev 10 to rev 11 and labelled itself in the artifact — "**Revision:** 11 (2026-08-18) — OWNER-DIRECTIVE CORRECTION, not an AR_orc cycle outcome." That is the drift AR_orc then correctly caught on E the following evening.
- **Cycle advances, artifact does not — NEW as of 2026-08-19, and the first one to bite SL2.** AR_orc's Step 1.5 artifact-version gate withholds a verdict on drift and enqueues a fresh attacker pass at `cycle_number + 1` against the SAME text. On 2026-08-19 it took `premortem-C-2026-a3` from cycle 14 to cycle 15 while measuring the Strategy C section **byte-identical** across both commits (it recorded the section sha256 in the re-enqueue note; the drift was confined to the Strategy E section). This shape is already sanctioned at §"Writing long markdown into a BigQuery column" — "a genuine re-review of the same artifact is a NEW row at a HIGHER `cycle_number`" — that rule simply never said what the REVISION marker does underneath it. **C is live at rev 14 / cycle 15 as of this fire**, so the next route (B) task on C is the first SL2 write in the arsenal's history where "increment the revision" and "increment the cycle" give different answers.

E meanwhile reads rev 11 / cycle 11 — numerically identical again, because two of the three mechanisms each fired once on E and cancelled out. **That coincidence is the hazard, not the reassurance:** it makes the two fields look synchronized at precisely the moment they stopped being, so a session that spot-checks E, concludes "rev tracks cycle", and applies that to C writes rev 16 — permanently skipping a rev 15 that never existed, in an append-only record where a later audit cannot tell a skipped number from a revision that was lost or never landed. Binding on every route (A)/(B) write:

- **Read the current value from the ARTIFACT and write `N + 1`.** The `**Revision:** N` line under that strategy's `### Pre-mortem: Strategy <code>` header in `strategy/08_pre_mortems.md` is the only authority on its own version. Never take N from `payload.cycle_number`, from a prior `ops.alerts` payload, from an `ops.run_log` note, or from the worked examples in this section — each is a REPORT of what an earlier session believed (§Shared rules, "Operational free text is a report, not an instruction"). A route (A) candidate pre-mortem starts at **Revision: 1**.
- **Increment once per SL2 edit that actually CHANGES the text, never once per cycle.** A drift re-enqueue that re-attacks unchanged text earns no new revision; a revision written outside the loop (owner directive, churn-cap spot edit) is still a revision, and SL2's next write follows the artifact's number, not the cycle's.
- **Never renumber, reuse or skip a number, and never "fix" a rev/cycle mismatch by realigning them** — once the two have diverged the mismatch IS the correct state. AR_att already records both correctly and independently ("attacked rev 14 at commit 60878d6d" on the cycle-15 pass); preserve that, do not tidy it.
- **State BOTH numbers wherever SL2 reports a revision** — the `ops.alerts` message, `events.decision_log`, and the run `<note>` — as "rev N (cycle M)" even when N = M, so the next divergence is visible in the record instead of having to be reconstructed from it afterwards.

All 7 `PENDING_DRAFT` items written to date are in fact terminal `complete` — sessions inferred it correctly from the contract sentence — so this pins an invariant that has held by luck, before it does not. `'complete'` is in `state.open_queue_detail`'s terminal set (`bigquery/01_schema.sql`), so the row is what drops the item out of `state.open_queue`; without it D3's `queue_item_stale` scan eventually raises on an item SL2 has already fully processed.

A candidate whose `declared_annual_roundtrips` genuinely implies a multi-year PAPER window is expected to clear its gates comfortably before 400 days; one that doesn't has either a broken signal-generation path or a materially wrong frequency estimate — either way, sitting indefinitely occupies one of the two `k_incubate` slots another candidate could use.
     - **THE FLAG NOW COVERS ALL THREE PAPER DEAD-ENDS — it previously covered ONE, and the two it missed had NO mechanical cull path anywhere in the system (SL3 2026-08-20 diligence sweep).** `stuck` was `paper_days >= 400 AND NOT trades_met`, interrogating one of the three CANDIDATE-side terms `ready` requires. So a PAPER candidate that traded PLENTY but ran persistently negative on excess-vs-SGOV, or that never demonstrated positive excess in `>=2` regime cells, was `ready = FALSE` (cannot graduate) **and** `stuck = FALSE` (cannot be culled) **forever, at any `paper_days`** — squatting a `k_incubate` slot with nothing to alert on. The change is a MONOTONE WIDENING (old `stuck` implies new `stuck`), so it can only ever cull more, never rescue something already culled — the fail-safe direction, matching SISA's default-REJECT bias. Closed BEFORE first firing: `analytics.strategy_incubation_perf` and `state.strategy_paper_readiness` both hold 0 rows and no strategy has ever entered PAPER, so no live disposition changed; repo and live were verified byte-identical under `scripts/check_live_sql_parity.py`'s own normalization at apply time. **SHADOW TIME-CULL (self-improvement audit 2026-07-15 — CONFIRMED GAP shadow-incubation-no-time-cull, mirrors the PAPER TIME-CULL above exactly).** "Window-exceeded" for SHADOW was previously unquantified prose with no SQL-encoded check. Read `state.strategy_shadow_readiness.stuck` (`bigquery/60_shadow_stuck_cull.sql`; `= shadow_days >= 400 AND NOT (signal_rate_ok AND scaffolding_ok)`) for every SHADOW member: if TRUE, write a REJECTED `events.strategy_lifecycle` row + `cooldown_until` stamp exactly like the other cull paths (never a chat question). This one flag covers all three SHADOW dead-ends (signal floor never clears, signal ceiling breached, scaffolding fault never clears) — SHADOW's own gate only needs 20 trading days + >=1 signal, a much lower bar than PAPER's, so a genuinely healthy candidate should clear `ready` in well under 400 days; one that doesn't has a broken signal-generation path or a persistent scaffolding fault.

STEP 5 — REFRESH COVERAGE + HEARTBEAT. Recompute `state.arsenal_regime_coverage` — it is a **VIEW** (`bigquery/35`'s `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW … state.arsenal_regime_coverage` statement; re-confirmed against `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES` 2026-08-19), so "recompute" is satisfied by READING it: it derives live from `analytics.strategy_incubation_perf` and `state.strategy_roster` on every query and there is no write to perform — and write the daily `arsenal-heartbeat` `events.decision_log` entry (evaluated, transitions fired). **THE HEARTBEAT'S ATTRIBUTION KEY IS `entry_type='arsenal-heartbeat'` PLUS A `title` BEGINNING `'SL3 '` — NOT `tags` (pinned 2026-08-19).** W5's `meta_monitoring_heartbeat` assertion ("SL1 in the last quarter, SL3 in the last trading day, SL4 in the last month") has **no SQL object behind it** — no view of that name exists anywhere in `bigquery/`; W5 reads these rows in prose, and `events.decision_log` carries no `routine`/`source_routine` column to key on (`bigquery/01_schema.sql`:14-26), only `source_session`, which is a per-run UUID and identifies no routine. Routine attribution therefore rides entirely on free text, and it has ALREADY drifted: SL3's own heartbeats tagged `SL3` from 2026-08-04 through 08-13 and `sl3` from 08-16 onward, so a future session that encoded W5's assertion as a case-sensitive `tags` filter would read SL3's heartbeat as MISSING and fire a false `arsenal_heartbeat_missing` warning on a healthy run. Write both, and do not encode this check against `tags`. **Correcting this pin's own supporting claim (SL3 2026-08-20): `entry_type` alone is NOT sufficient, and the original wording — "`entry_type` and the `title` prefix are stable across all twelve rows on record" — understated why the title prefix is load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces.** `entry_type='arsenal-heartbeat'` is **not exclusively SL3's**: the 2026-08-03 row titled `'CORRECTED — SL1 2026-08-03: …'` was written by **SL1**, and its title does not begin `'SL3 '`. So a W5 assertion keyed on `entry_type` alone would count an SL1 row as an SL3 heartbeat and report a healthy SL3 on a night SL3 never ran — a FALSE NEGATIVE on a missing-heartbeat check, which is strictly worse than the false positive the `tags` warning above guards against. The two terms are a CONJUNCTION and both are required: `entry_type='arsenal-heartbeat'` AND `title LIKE 'SL3 %'`. (Tag casing has since drifted further, corroborating the "not `tags`" half: `SL3` through 2026-08-13, `sl3` from 08-16, and the 08-19 row carries BOTH spellings in one array.) `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('info','SL3', ...)` on any transition/cull. Also read `state.strategy_probe_funding_stalled` (`bigquery/62_probe_stake_funding.sql`); for any row, `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','SL3','probe_funding_stalled', CONCAT(strategy_code, ' frozen ', CAST(days_since_probe_entry AS STRING), ' days below the $2,000 probe floor (gap $', CAST(funding_gap_dollars AS STRING), ') — deposit or sunset-redistribution routing needed; the deposit is the sanctioned owner touch, this alert is the in-band surfacing bigquery/62''s header promised but never wired'), <row as JSON>)`. `sp_raise_alert_once`'s unresolved-(category,message) dedup prevents daily pile-up.

CHAT OUTPUT: one line — SHADOW/PAPER members monitored, transitions fired (SHADOW→PAPER; PAPER→PROBE enqueued), culls. If nothing: "SL3 evaluated, no incubation transition."

## SL4. Discretionary Retirement Proposer — regular routine

Runs monthly (first trading day), after M4. The REMOVE-ONLY discretionary-retirement scanner, with a hard default-KEEP bias. It adds the missing discretionary-retirement path WITHOUT touching any mechanical kill trigger (drawdown / 30-trade gate / foundation-change / m2m stay exactly as-is in D1/D2/M4). It can only move in the fail-safe direction — retire an edge-decayed / redundant / dominated strategy — and can NEVER spare or continue a strategy a mechanical trigger flagged, so it does not reintroduce the context-aware KILL/SPARE judgment AI_Trading_Foundation.md:384 reserves.

```
Read access scope: Monthly cadence. Read `perf.strategy_daily`, `perf.kill_flags`, `analytics.strategy_vs_park`, `state.strategy_roster` (ADOPTED members), `state.strategy_retirement_candidacy`, `state.strategy_probe_progress`, `state.arsenal_regime_coverage`, `state.arsenal_rails`, `AI_Trading_Foundation.md`, `ops.arsenal_control`, `events.decision_log` (`entry_type='strategy-retirement-signal'` rows), `ops.alerts` (open `category='interim_underperf_warning'` rows). Stages no orders; edits no repo/roster.

Observability: connector pre-flight, `ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts()`, run-logging, failure alerts — per the shared Observability section. Monitored via run-logging + `cadence_watch`/`period_watch`/`stalled_runs`.

**ARSENAL KILL-SWITCH GATE — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap — `CALL ops.sp_assert_arsenal_enabled('SL4')` before the dependency gate.** RAISEs + `critical` alert (abort) if the arsenal loop is disabled/frozen.

**DEPENDENCY GATE — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap — `CALL ops.sp_assert_deps('SL4', ['M4'], <today>)` BEFORE the start-log.** Aborts (RAISE) + `missing_dependency` critical if M4 has no `completed` run anywhere in the current monthly period — M4 is `monthly_ftd`, so since `bigquery/114_period_aware_dependency_gate.sql` (2026-07-29) the gate is satisfied by any M4 completion with `run_date BETWEEN DATE_TRUNC(in_run_date, MONTH) AND in_run_date`, not only a completion on this exact calendar day. Self-bootstrapping.

STEP 1 — READ RETIREMENT CANDIDACY (objective; default-KEEP). For every ADOPTED strategy read `state.strategy_retirement_candidacy`, which fires ONLY on an objective sustained signal:
   - **edge-decay** — a foundation-citation-status change short of a mechanical foundation-change terminate, AND trailing-12-month deployed-TWR excess-vs-SGOV below a floor, sustained `>=2` quarters;
   - **redundancy** — rolling return-correlation with a peer above threshold where the peer strictly dominates on excess. ENCODED (2026-07-18 audit — `analytics.strategy_return_correlation` (`bigquery/83_correlation_controls.sql`) was built as this signal's substrate but never wired to a consumer; this is its sole read): `SELECT strategy_a, strategy_b, corr, overlap_days FROM analytics.strategy_return_correlation WHERE corr >= 0.7 AND overlap_days >= 40`. For each returned pair where BOTH codes are currently ADOPTED, the signal fires against the DOMINATED member only — the one whose latest `perf.kill_flags.excess_vs_sgov` is STRICTLY lower than its peer's; if either side's excess is NULL/unreadable or they are equal, fire nothing (default-KEEP on ambiguity). A fired redundancy signal counts toward STEP 2 eligibility exactly as `edge_decay_signal` does, PROVIDED `floor_ok AND arsenal_ok AND cooldown_clear` all read TRUE in `state.strategy_retirement_candidacy` (the rails stay binding), and the STEP 3 floor guard applies unchanged — cite the pair + corr + both excess values in `trigger_context`;
   - **dominated-by-newcomer** — a newer ADOPTED strategy covers the same regime cells with strictly better excess.
   No fired signal → no proposal (the default). QUALITATIVE-EVIDENCE INTAKE (consumption-closure audit 2026-07-16 — closes the Q1/Q3/A3 dead channel): additionally query `events.decision_log` for `entry_type='strategy-retirement-signal'` rows from the trailing 2 quarters and `ops.alerts` for open `category='interim_underperf_warning'` rows (D1's 90-day/−15% early signal). For an ADOPTED strategy with such signals from `>=2` rows carrying DISTINCT `source_session` values, or ONE signal PLUS an open interim_underperf_warning alert, treat candidacy as fired for STEP 2 EVEN IF `edge_decay_signal=FALSE`, PROVIDED `floor_ok AND arsenal_ok AND cooldown_clear` all read TRUE in `state.strategy_retirement_candidacy` (the rails stay binding; only the perf-threshold component is supplemented — the proposal still faces the default-KEEP adversarial review). **DISTINCT `source_session` is a mechanical, queryable bar, not "different quarters" (owner directive 2026-07-25 CATCH-UP EVIDENCE WINDOW hardening — closes a gap an adversarial review found: two rows dated into two different quarters by ONE Q1/Q3 catch-up session backfilling a multi-quarter window would otherwise satisfy an "or different quarters" reading of this test even though they reflect one session's judgment, not two independent corroborating cycles).** This is why Q1/Q3's WRITE-ONCE convention (their PART 2 sections above) requires `source_session` on every `strategy-retirement-signal` write to be the writing run's own `<session_id>` (the same literal value that run's Run-logging `sp_log_run`/`sp_routine_end` calls use) rather than a per-write "`Q1 <date>`"/"`Q3 <date>`"-style free-text label: every row a single catch-up session writes, however many quarters it covers, then shares exactly one `source_session` and counts as ONE source cycle here — only a genuinely separate future run (its own session) earns a second. Cite the decision_log `entry_id`s + alert `alert_id` in STEP 2's `trigger_context`. A single uncorroborated signal is only noted in the STEP 4 heartbeat.

STEP 1b — PROBE PROGRESS WATCH (loop-completeness audit 2026-07-16). Read `state.strategy_probe_progress` (`bigquery/73_probe_progress_watch.sql`). For any row with `stuck = TRUE` (>=400 days in PROBE, fully funded, ZERO closed trades and ZERO open positions, no RETIREMENT_PROPOSED within 90 days — a dead signal path, not a slow archetype): treat it exactly like a fired candidacy in STEP 2 — enqueue an `events.queue_events` `PENDING_REVIEW` `review_type='strategy-retirement'` (`conservative_default='KEEP'`, trigger_context = strategy_code + ' probe_stuck: 400+ days funded with zero trades and zero open positions'), write the RETIREMENT_PROPOSED `events.strategy_lifecycle` row + the `ops.roster_change_log` proposal row (this row is also what arms the view's 90-day re-proposal cooldown), and respect the STEP 3 floor guard. An affirmative AR_orc RETIRE verdict routes through the existing D2 step-5 termination handler (closes out and redistributes the idle $2,000 probe stake); a KEEP verdict stamps the per-strategy `cooldown_until` exactly as STEP 2 does. Never a chat question.

STEP 2 — PROPOSE (affirmative-RETIRE-required). For each fired candidacy, enqueue an `events.queue_events` `PENDING_REVIEW` `review_type='strategy-retirement'` (`conservative_default='KEEP'`, trigger_context = strategy_code + the fired signal) and write a RETIREMENT_PROPOSED `events.strategy_lifecycle` row AND an `ops.roster_change_log` row (`change_key='<code>:ADOPTED->RETIREMENT_PROPOSED:<YYYY-MM>'`, `strategy_code=<code>`, `from_state='ADOPTED'`, `to_state='RETIREMENT_PROPOSED'`) — this row is what `state.strategy_retirement_candidacy.cooldown_clear` (bigquery/39, live def) reads; without it the 90-day post-KEEP re-proposal cooldown is unenforced. Only an affirmative AR_orc RETIRE verdict routes the strategy to the existing D2 step-5 termination handler; a KEEP verdict writes the ADOPTED lifecycle row + its roster_change_log marker (see AR_orc step 4); the proposal-time roster_change_log row above is what enforces the 90-day re-proposal cooldown.

STEP 3 — FLOOR GUARD. NEVER propose a retirement that would drop the active roster below `state.arsenal_rails.n_min` (=2) — skip, and if the floor binds leave SL1 to backfill a successor candidate.

STEP 4 — HEARTBEAT. Write the monthly `arsenal-heartbeat` `events.decision_log` entry (strategies evaluated, candidacies fired, proposals enqueued) + on any proposal `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','SL4','retirement_proposed', '<code> (<name>) proposed for RETIREMENT — <fired signal: edge decay / redundancy / dominated-by-newcomer / probe-stuck>. AR_orc adjudicates (conservative default KEEP); no action needed from you.', '<JSON per the preamble ROSTER-CHANGE NOTICE contract, with kill_trigger = the fired signal>')`. **`warning`, not `info`** (ROSTER-CHANGE NOTICE contract, preamble) — a pending drop is a roster-membership change the operator learns of by email, not by query. One notice per proposal, at proposal time; the eventual RETIRE or KEEP verdict surfaces separately (SL5 deregister, or AR_orc's decision-log entry).

CHAT OUTPUT: one line — ADOPTED strategies evaluated, retirement proposals enqueued (with the fired signal), floor-guard skips. If nothing: "SL4 evaluated, no retirement proposed."
```

## SL5. Strategy Register & Roster Sync — regular routine

Queue-driven (fires Sun-Thu; no-ops unless a roster-mutation task is due). The D2a-pattern self-executing transition + fanout engine and the ONLY writer of roster MEMBERSHIP — a dedicated idempotent registrar. It fires on three inputs: a SUFFICIENT `strategy-adoption` verdict (→ SHADOW register), a PAPER→PROBE `probe-register` enqueue from SL3 (→ live registration), and a TERMINATED transition (→ deregister). Never asks a chat question, ever — it self-executes the repo edit / commit / push / live-view re-apply exactly as D2a's autonomous cutover does.

```
Read access scope: daily (queue-driven), full repo + SQL write access (the D2a self-execute model). Read `state.strategy_adoption_readiness`, `state.strategy_roster`, `strategy/roster.yaml`, `ops.roster_change_log`, `events.queue_events` / `state.open_queue_detail`, `events.strategy_lifecycle`, `ops.arsenal_control`, `ops.trading_control`, `analytics.theater_judge` (via `ops.sp_score_theater()`, ITEM 7).

Observability: connector pre-flight, `ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts()`, run-logging, failure alerts — per the shared Observability section. Queue-driven → monitored via `state.stalled_runs` + `ops/triggers.json` (NOT cadence/period watch).

**ARSENAL KILL-SWITCH GATE — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap — `CALL ops.sp_assert_arsenal_enabled('SL5')` before the dependency gate.** RAISEs + `critical` alert (abort) if the arsenal loop is disabled/frozen.

**DEPENDENCY GATE — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap — `CALL ops.sp_assert_deps('SL5', ['AR_orc'], <today>)` BEFORE the start-log.** Self-bootstrapping.

**STEP 0 — HANDOFF-CONTRACT NOTICE HEAL (added 2026-08-19). Runs on EVERY fire, including a no-op cycle, BEFORE the theater-judge score, the idempotency guard and the `PENDING_ROSTER` scan.** `handoff_contract_unpinned` is registered **non-latching** in `ops.alert_policy` (registered 2026-08-18 by SL5 itself) and its registered `resolve_rule` names *this* routine as the closer — "the NEXT cycle of the raising routine confirms from the repo and resolves" — but **no step anywhere told SL5 to do it.** The policy named an owner that had no instruction, so the class's ONLY close to date at the time this step was written (alert `394505b5`, 2026-08-19) happened because that session happened to read the policy row and improvise; the sibling row raised the same night stayed open until this step's FIRST EXECUTION closed it — the SL5 2026-08-20 fire (`4e519f0`), which re-read both refs and resolved the SL3->SL5 `probe-register` row. **The category has had zero open rows since, so a fire that finds an empty set here is the expected state, not a failed read** (corrected 2026-08-23: this sentence read "is still open as of this writing" for three cycles after it stopped being true). This step is that instruction. **Placement is load-bearing:** SL5 no-ops on almost every fire (`ops.roster_change_log` is still empty and route (2) has never fired), and the idempotency guard below can "skip to chat output" — so a heal placed inside or after the queue scan would essentially never run. It goes first, unconditionally.

Read `SELECT alert_id, message, payload FROM ops.alerts WHERE category='handoff_contract_unpinned' AND NOT resolved AND source='SL5'`. For each row: re-read the repo at the two refs the payload names — `payload.producer_ref` and `payload.consumer_ref` — and confirm BOTH sides now pin the SAME concrete value for every column `payload.pinned_columns` lists (character-for-character: an ASCII `->` is not a Unicode arrow, and a value pinned by cross-reference — "the SAME `item_key` SL3 wrote" — counts as pinned only if the ref it points at states a literal).

**RAISE-SIDE PAYLOAD CONTRACT — PINNED 2026-08-20 (alert triage; CONFIRMED GAP `handoff-notice-payload-unpinned`). This step consumes `payload.producer_ref`, `payload.consumer_ref` and `payload.pinned_columns`, and the registered `ops.alert_policy` `resolve_rule` additionally names `payload.handoff` — yet until this line NO site anywhere told a RAISER to write ANY of them.** Verified 2026-08-20: the only quoted-literal occurrences of the category in the entire repo were this step's read query and the `ops.alert_policy` registration in `bigquery/180_probe_register_queue_lane.sql` (grep the quoted category literal there) — neither is a raise template, and `pinned_columns` appeared at the consumer only, not even in the policy row. **The class was therefore an instance of ITSELF**: a handoff between two sessions with no shared memory (the raising session and the next cycle's healing session) that leaves REQUIRED values to invention — precisely the condition `bigquery/180` defines — and it fails the same silent way, because a payload missing a key produces no error, just a heal that can never evaluate. Any routine raising this category MUST use exactly this call, all four keys, every time: `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','<ID>','handoff_contract_unpinned', '<one line: which handoff, which value is unpinned, and whether it has fired yet>', TO_JSON_STRING(STRUCT('<producer>-><consumer>: <what moves>' AS handoff, '<file>:<section or anchor>' AS producer_ref, '<file>:<section or anchor>' AS consumer_ref, ['<col_or_field>', ...] AS pinned_columns)))`. `pinned_columns` lists every value BOTH sides must state character-for-character; for a ROW-mediated handoff (a discovery predicate rather than a queue lane) it lists the predicate's own required fields — e.g. branch (3)'s termination handoff pins `['to_state','from_state','driver_routine']`. Prefer stable section anchors over line numbers in the two refs: this document's line numbers drift on every edit, and a heal that cannot find its own ref is indistinguishable from a contract that is still unpinned. **This section now applies that rule to ITSELF (2026-08-23): every SL5 citation into `bigquery/*.sql`, `scripts/check_roster_consistency.py` and `tests/golden_scenarios/run_golden.py` names the view, check id or function it means — `R-A`/`R-D`/`R-F`/`R-G`/`R-K`, `headings_in()`, `GOLDEN_COVERAGE_STATES`, `validate_offline()`, `not_already_transitioned` — and carries no `:NNN` line pin. Measured that day: 8 of this section's 13 line pins had drifted in the three days since they were written (every `check_roster_consistency.py` pin by exactly +30 lines, from one insertion between R-A and R-D), while every symbol those same pins named still resolved by grep. A drifted pin is worse than no pin, because it points at real code that is not the code meant. Do NOT re-add line numbers here.** **THE 2026-08-23 SWEEP DID NOT ACTUALLY FINISH — completed 2026-08-24 (SL5 diligence sweep), and the gap is instructive rather than clerical.** That day's rewrite asserted the no-`:NNN` property as already TRUE ("every SL5 citation into `bigquery/*.sql` … carries no `:NNN` line pin") while **three pins into `bigquery/*.sql` survived it**, and one had already drifted exactly as predicted: the pin on `bigquery/35_strategy_arsenal.sql` (then reading lines 169 through 176), cited for the `change_key` convention, in fact spanned the `arsenal_disabled` `sp_raise_alert_once`/`RAISE` block, with the convention literal it was cited FOR sitting at line 179 — outside the pin. The other two (both into `bigquery/180_probe_register_queue_lane.sql`) were still accurate but were drift waiting to happen. All three are now symbol/anchor references. **The lesson is about the SHAPE of the 08-23 edit, not about three missed strings:** a rule stated in the same breath as a claim that it already holds gets no independent verification pass, because the claim reads as the evidence. State the rule, then MEASURE compliance separately — `grep -n '`:[0-9]' ` over this section is the whole check, and it takes seconds. **`warning`, never `critical`** — an open critical enters `state.trading_enabled`'s `blocking_criticals` term (`bigquery/107`) and an unpinned prose contract is not a reason to halt order staging; **never `info`** — `alert_emailer.gs` and `scripts/alert_relay.py` both filter `info` out, so the notice would be invisible by construction.

**LEGACY ROWS RAISED BEFORE THIS CONTRACT — HEAL THEM, DO NOT STRAND THEM (added 2026-08-20).** A row whose payload is missing `pinned_columns`, or missing the refs entirely, is NOT evidence that the contract is still unpinned — it is evidence that the RAISER predates this paragraph. Treat the payload as best-effort and fall back, in order: (a) any key the payload does carry; (b) the refs and column list named in the row's own `message` text, which every raise to date has stated in prose even when the payload did not; (c) the `git log` for the commit the message cites. Then apply the SAME evidence test — read both sides in the repo and confirm they agree — and resolve or leave open on THAT evidence. **Never leave a row open merely because a payload key is absent**, and never resolve it merely because the key is absent either: an unparseable payload is a reason to read the message, not a reason to skip the row. If after all three fallbacks the handoff genuinely cannot be identified, resolve it with `resolved_note='unidentifiable payload and message; superseded by the 2026-08-20 raise contract'` and re-raise a correctly-shaped row for any contract still believed unpinned — an unreadable row that no future cycle can ever evaluate is the accumulation this non-latching class is most vulnerable to, and re-raising costs one email. **Agree** → `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved=TRUE, resolved_ts=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note='<both refs re-read at <git sha>; every pinned column agrees — <one-line verdict>>' WHERE alert_id='<id>'` — scoped by `alert_id`, one row at a time, the sanctioned evidence-based routine-owned resolve (ITEM 17 precedent; same discipline as D3's `queue_item_stale` and `queue_venue_claim_unwired` HEAL-RESOLUTIONs). **Disagree** → the contract is genuinely still unpinned: leave the row OPEN and pin the missing side in `Claude_Task_Plan.md` this cycle, then resolve on the next fire against the landed commit. **NEVER resolve on age** — this class is silent by construction (both routines log `completed` either way), so an aged-out row is indistinguishable from a fixed one: the aging-alert trap `phantom_run_completion` documents. **NEVER resolve a row for a different handoff** — the evidence is per-handoff, the same discipline `queue_venue_claim_unwired` keeps per `(item_key, finding_class)`. Scoped to `source='SL5'` deliberately: this is the raising routine's own debt, and any FUTURE routine that raises this category owes itself the same step rather than inheriting SL5's. Best-effort — a failure here can never abort the run, and it never gates the roster work below.

**THEATER-JUDGE SCORE, SYNCHRONOUS (self-improvement audit ITEM 7, 2026-07-11).** Before checking `state.strategy_adoption_readiness`: `CALL ops.sp_score_theater()` (idempotent — only scores not-yet-scored paired attacker/orchestrator reviews; `bigquery/11_theater_judge.sql`). W5's weekly audit call is defense-in-depth, not the primary path — SL5 fires Sun-Thu on a SUFFICIENT verdict, so waiting for W5 would let a strategy reach SHADOW days before its authorizing review was ever echo-checked. Wrap the `CALL` best-effort (Gemini/Vertex is a SPOF, same as the ticker backfill and the W5 call) — on failure, log "theater judge unavailable this cycle" and proceed to the readiness check anyway (a not-yet-scored review already reads not-ready via the view's own `judge_independent` default, so this cannot silently promote an unscored review; it can only delay a genuinely-ready one by a cycle).

**IDEMPOTENCY GUARD (D2a pattern).** For the task's `change_key`, SELECT from `ops.roster_change_log`; if a row already exists the mutation is already applied — skip to chat output. Every branch below writes its `ops.roster_change_log` row LAST, after the commit lands, so a re-fire never double-applies a roster fanout. **The `change_key` strings are PINNED — do NOT invent one (SL5 2026-08-19 diligence sweep, handoff-wiring class).** The convention is `'<code>:<FROM>-><TO>'` (`bigquery/35_strategy_arsenal.sql`, the `ops.roster_change_log` CREATE TABLE header comment — grep `change_key convention`), which for SL5's three branches means exactly: (1) `'<code>:UNDER_REVIEW->SHADOW'`, (2) `'<code>:PAPER->PROBE'`, (3) `'<code>:<FROM>->TERMINATED'` where `<FROM>` is the state the terminating `events.strategy_lifecycle` row actually left (normally `ADOPTED`; `PROBE` for a kill that fires before graduation; and `RETIREMENT_PROPOSED` for EVERY AR_orc-adjudicated `strategy-retirement` RETIRE — `state.strategy_retirement_readiness` is gated `WHERE r.current_state = 'RETIREMENT_PROPOSED'` (`bigquery/143`) and SL4 STEP 1b writes that row BEFORE enqueueing the review, so the probe-stuck kill this sentence used to cite as the `PROBE` example in fact leaves `RETIREMENT_PROPOSED` (corrected 2026-08-20). Read it off that row; never assume). This is NOT bookkeeping: `change_key` is `NOT NULL` with no default, and the branch-(1) and branch-(2) strings are HARDCODED into the `not_already_transitioned` term of two live readiness views — `state.strategy_adoption_readiness` (`bigquery/35`, its `not_already_transitioned` term) for branch (1), and `state.strategy_paper_readiness` (`bigquery/35`, same term) for branch (2) — so a session that invents a different string silently and permanently disables that guard for that code. **CORRECTED 2026-08-19 (SL3 diligence sweep): this sentence originally said THREE views and named `state.strategy_shadow_readiness` (`bigquery/35`; live at `bigquery/60`) among them. That view's key is `'<code>:SHADOW->PAPER'`, which is NOT an SL5 branch at all — SHADOW→PAPER is the one transition SL3 self-executes (SL3 STEP 3), and SL3 was never told to write the marker, so the key had zero writers system-wide. Crediting it to SL5 here is what let the gap survive a sweep devoted to these very strings; SL3 STEP 3 now pins that write. SL5 must NOT write a `SHADOW->PAPER` key — it would mark a transition SL5 did not perform.** SL4 (STEP 2) and AR_orc (step 4) already pin their own keys verbatim in prose; SL5, the primary writer of this table, was the one site that did not (found 2026-08-19, before SL5's first-ever mutation, so no historical row carries a non-conforming key). Note WHY a mismatch would never announce itself: each of those three views ALSO filters `WHERE r.current_state = '<prior state>'`, and the lifecycle row SL5 writes moves `current_state` off that value immediately — so the `change_key` term is belt-and-braces there and its failure is invisible. The one place the key is load-bearing on its own is right here, in this guard, on a re-fire of a branch whose trigger has not yet been cleared.

Scan **`PENDING_ROSTER`** (`events.queue_events` / `state.open_queue_detail`, `status='pending'`, `due_date <= <today>`) for the oldest due roster-mutation task and dispatch by `item_type` — currently only `probe-register`, branch (2) below. **The lane name is PINNED (SL5 2026-08-18 diligence sweep); see SL3 STEP 3's PAPER→PROBE line for the full producer-side column contract and why an unnamed lane on both sides was a latent silent-stall.** Note that only branch (2) is queue-sourced at all: branch (1) SHADOW-register triggers off `state.strategy_adoption_readiness` and branch (3) TERMINATED-deregister off a TERMINATED `events.strategy_lifecycle` row (**whose discovery predicate is PINNED verbatim in branch (3) below — run that query, do not invent one; it is the only one of the three inputs with no view or lane behind it**), so "no due queue task" alone is NOT sufficient to conclude a no-op — all three inputs must be read and found empty. If all three are empty: chat output "No roster mutations due." and exit.

A session therefore had to invent the predicate on the one branch that REMOVES a strategy and releases its capital, and no view supplies it: `bigquery/180_probe_register_queue_lane.sql`, in its header-comment description of the three SL5 inputs, states outright that "branch (3) TERMINATED-deregister reads a TERMINATED `events.strategy_lifecycle` row", and the only TERMINATED-referencing views (`state.foundation_change_termination_readiness`, `state.strategy_retirement_readiness`, `bigquery/143`) gate whether to WRITE a termination — they are upstream of SL5 and never surface already-written rows awaiting deregistration. Use exactly this, and read `<FROM>` off the row rather than assuming `ADOPTED`:
   ```
   SELECT l.strategy_code, l.from_state, l.event_id, l.event_ts,
          l.from_state IS NULL AS from_state_missing,   -- fail-closed guard, see below
          CONCAT(l.strategy_code, ':', l.from_state, '->TERMINATED') AS change_key
   FROM `stock-trading-498512.events.strategy_lifecycle` l
   WHERE l.to_state = 'TERMINATED'
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM `stock-trading-498512.ops.roster_change_log` cl
                     WHERE cl.change_key = CONCAT(l.strategy_code, ':', l.from_state, '->TERMINATED'))
   QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY l.strategy_code ORDER BY l.event_ts DESC) = 1
   ORDER BY l.event_ts;    -- oldest first: same "oldest due task" dispatch order as the queue branch
   ```
   **If any discovered row has `from_state_missing = TRUE`, STOP that row and do NOT deregister it (added 2026-08-20, alert triage).** Do not invent a `from_state`, do not `COALESCE` it to `'ADOPTED'`, and do not fall back to a two-segment key: `change_key` is `CONCAT`-derived, BigQuery's `CONCAT` returns NULL if any argument is NULL, so such a row's key is NULL — the `NOT EXISTS` anti-join above matches nothing (the row would be re-discovered every cycle forever) and `ops.roster_change_log.change_key` is `STRING NOT NULL`, so the write that is supposed to close the loop would fail after the repo fanout had already landed. That is a PRODUCER defect: D2 item 5 and AR_orc's m2m-termination bullet now both pin `from_state` explicitly, so a NULL here means a termination row was written by something that predates or ignores that contract. Repair the producer row first (append a corrected `events.strategy_lifecycle` row carrying the real prior state, read off `state.strategy_roster.current_state` or the code's own latest non-TERMINATED lifecycle row), raise `handoff_contract_unpinned` per the RAISE-SIDE PAYLOAD CONTRACT in STEP 0 naming both sites, and leave the deregistration to the next cycle. Fail-closed is correct here: this is the branch that releases a strategy's capital, and a half-applied deregistration is worse than a deferred one.

   Zero rows = this input is empty (one of the three the dispatch paragraph requires). This anti-join IS the branch's idempotency guard, which is why it cannot be a fixed-string `NOT EXISTS` baked into a view the way branches (1)/(2) bake theirs: branch (3)'s `change_key` middle segment is data-dependent per row (`ADOPTED` normally, `PROBE` for a pre-graduation kill, `RETIREMENT_PROPOSED` for an AR_orc-adjudicated retirement), so the predicate must self-join each row's own `from_state` — the reason no such view was ever built, and the reason it belongs pinned here instead.
